places.name: Country Park
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: 3905 Nathanael Greene Drive, Greensboro, NC 27455
places.summary: Country Park is Greensboro's historic lake and recreation park within the Battleground Parks District, with paved and natural trails, playgrounds, dog park, fishing piers, picnic shelters, restrooms, canopy walk, seasonal pedal boats, carousel, and zipline.
places.hours: Park hours change seasonally and with weather; verify the posted closing time before a late visit. Seasonal boats, carousel, zipline, and neighboring attractions use separate hours.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, dog-park, and picnic access is free. Fishing passes, pedal boats, carousel, zipline, reservations, and adjacent attractions may charge.
places.parking: Use 3905 Nathanael Greene Drive, the Orman Road lot, or 3805 Jaycee Park Drive depending on your destination. The internal loop road is reserved for pedestrians and cyclists.
places.restroom: Accessible restrooms are available near developed recreation areas, including the playground and shelters. Remote trail sections do not have continuous facilities.
places.accessibility: Most major features are reasonably accessible, including fishing dock, playground, restrooms, shelters 1 and 2, and an all-persons nature trail. The Orman Road lot is recommended for many visitors using mobility devices.
places.trail: The park has 1.67 miles of paved trail plus nature, hiking, biking, and mountain-bike routes. Surfaces, slopes, roots, and weather conditions vary outside the paved loop.
places.family: Families can use playgrounds, the canopy walk, fishing piers, picnic areas, and seasonal pedal boats, carousel, and zipline. Paid and seasonal attractions should be checked separately.
places.dogs: The park has separate large- and small-dog off-leash areas. Dogs must be leashed again outside the designated dog park and kept clear of restricted attractions.
places.picnic: Five picnic shelters are available; reserve a shelter for guaranteed group use. Casual picnicking remains possible in permitted areas when space is available.
places.landmarks: Key destinations include the two fishing lakes, Guilford County Veterans Memorial, canopy walk, playgrounds, dog park, and connections into the Battleground Parks District.
places.closures: Weather, lake conditions, trail maintenance, major events, and seasonal attraction schedules can affect individual areas. Check the City page and on-site signs before traveling for one exact feature.

places.name: Battleground Parks District
places.operator: City of Greensboro and district partners
places.address: 3905 Nathanael Greene Drive, Greensboro, NC 27455
places.summary: Battleground Parks District is a 400-acre connected history, science, and recreation district with more than 13 miles of trails linking Country Park, Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, Greensboro Science Center, Jaycee Park, Lewis Recreation Center, Forest Lawn, and Spencer Love Tennis Center.
places.hours: The district is visitable year-round, but every component has its own gates, hours, holidays, programs, and event schedule. Check the exact destination rather than relying on one district-wide time.
places.cost: Outdoor district trails, Country Park, and the national military park are generally free. Greensboro Science Center, carousel, zipline, rentals, programs, and some recreation facilities charge separately.
places.parking: There is no single district lot. Start at Country Park, Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, Greensboro Science Center, Jaycee Park, or another named destination based on the visit.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at staffed or developed component destinations, not continuously across all 400 acres and 13 miles of trail. Confirm the facility nearest your route.
places.accessibility: Accessible options exist at Country Park, the national military park, science center, recreation facilities, and developed trailheads, but routes differ between operators and natural trail segments.
places.trail: More than 13 miles of trails and greenways connect the district. Expect a mix of paved shared-use routes and natural trails, plus road crossings and destination-specific rules.
places.family: Families can combine playgrounds and lakes at Country Park, exhibits at Greensboro Science Center, Revolutionary War history, tennis, recreation facilities, and trails. Admission and hours differ by stop.
places.dogs: Dog rules depend on the component. Country Park includes a dog park, while the national military park, science center, indoor facilities, and events may have different restrictions.
places.picnic: Country Park provides the district's clearest shelter and picnic options. Reservations, group activities, and food rules vary at other district destinations.
places.landmarks: The district's primary landmarks are Country Park, Greensboro Science Center, Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, Forest Lawn, Jaycee Park, Lewis Recreation Center, and Spencer Love Tennis Center.
places.closures: Closures can be component-specific because the district has several operators. Verify national park notices, City trail alerts, science-center hours, and event impacts for the exact itinerary.

places.name: LeBauer Park
places.operator: Greensboro Downtown Parks Inc. in partnership with the City of Greensboro
places.address: 208 North Davie Street, Greensboro, NC 27401
places.summary: LeBauer Park is a downtown Greensboro destination with an inclusive playground, seasonal interactive fountains, sensory space, dog park, gardens, food kiosks, great lawn, performance space, restrooms, games, and major public art.
places.hours: The park is normally open daily from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. unless otherwise posted. The seasonal splash plaza normally operates May through September from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.
places.cost: General park, playground, garden, lawn, public-art, dog-park, and seasonal fountain access is free. Food, rentals, programs, and ticketed events may charge.
places.parking: Use a legal downtown street space, public garage, transit stop, or destination-specific accessible arrival near North Davie Street. Event days can change street and garage availability.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are listed among the park's accessible amenities. Hours and access may be affected by maintenance or special events.
places.accessibility: The City identifies the cafes, performance place, great lawn, playground, aerial sculpture, fountains, sensory space, dog park, gardens, games, and restrooms as reasonably accessible by mobility device.
places.trail: LeBauer is a compact paved downtown park rather than a hiking destination. Paved paths connect its lawns, play areas, gardens, public art, and neighboring Center City Park.
places.family: The inclusive playground, Lincoln Financial Children's Garden, Peacehaven Sensory Space, lawn, games, and seasonal interactive fountains make this a strong family stop.
places.dogs: A designated dog park is available. Dogs should remain controlled elsewhere in the park and may be restricted from fountains, play areas, food service, or programmed events.
places.picnic: Visitors can eat in public park areas and purchase food nearby, but organized or exclusive gatherings require approval through Greensboro Downtown Parks Inc.
places.landmarks: Look for Janet Echelman's aerial sculpture Where We Met, the Women's Holocaust Memorial, Carolyn's Garden, the sensory space, great lawn, and performance place.
places.closures: Special events, fountain maintenance, severe weather, private rentals, and downtown street closures can affect individual areas. Check the downtown parks schedule before an event-specific visit.

places.name: Greensboro Arboretum
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: 401 Ashland Drive, Greensboro, NC 27403
places.summary: Greensboro Arboretum is a free 17-acre public garden in Lindley Park with 14 plant collections, paved walking paths, display gardens, rose garden, wedding gazebo, scenic overlook, bridges, fountain, and restrooms.
places.hours: The public garden follows posted seasonal park closing times and is weather dependent. It is closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas; confirm the current closing time before an evening visit.
places.cost: Casual public garden access is free. Garden reservations and paid professional photography require fees and permits; a reservation does not make the whole garden exclusive.
places.parking: Use on-street parking on Ashland Drive or the West Market ballfield lot at 3299 Starmount Drive. Choose the side closest to the garden feature you need.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are listed as an accessible garden feature. Availability can change with maintenance and seasonal park operations.
places.accessibility: The paved walking trail, public garden, and restrooms are identified as reasonably accessible by mobility device. Some garden edges and secondary surfaces may differ.
places.trail: A paved walking trail connects the 17-acre garden and its collections. This is a garden stroll rather than a long natural-surface hike.
places.family: Families can explore plant collections, bridges, fountain, overlook, arbor, and changing seasonal displays. Supervise children around water, plants, events, and photography sessions.
places.dogs: Follow posted City garden rules for pets and keep any permitted dog leashed and out of planted beds. Special events or reserved garden areas may be more restrictive.
places.picnic: Use designated public areas without blocking paths or reserved events. Contact the City for weddings, professional photography, exclusive setups, or organized gatherings.
places.landmarks: Highlights include the Kaplan Family Rose Garden, landmark arbor, wedding gazebo, scenic overlook, fountain, bridges, and 14 permanent plant collections.
places.closures: Weather, horticultural work, weddings, events, photography, and seasonal closing times can affect access to individual features. Check posted notices before a feature-specific visit.

places.name: Bog Garden at Benjamin Park
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1101 Hobbs Road, Greensboro, NC 27410
places.summary: Bog Garden at Benjamin Park is a seven-acre wetland garden known for its elevated wooden boardwalk, native habitat, wildlife, and Serenity Falls recirculating waterfall.
places.hours: The garden is currently closed for construction until further notice. Normal hours begin at 8 a.m. with seasonal closing times when the City reopens it.
places.cost: Ordinary garden access is free when open. Event reservations and paid professional photography require fees or permits.
places.parking: The garden is at 1101 Hobbs Road opposite Tanger Family Bicentennial Garden. Do not travel for parking or boardwalk access until the City removes the construction closure.
places.restroom: Do not rely on garden facilities while the site is closed. After reopening, confirm restroom availability and the best accessible route on the current City page.
places.accessibility: The signature route is an elevated boardwalk through wetlands. Construction may change surfaces, railings, approaches, and accessible routing, so reassess after reopening.
places.trail: The principal experience is an elevated wood-plank boardwalk through seven acres of wetlands. It is not currently accessible because the garden is closed for construction.
places.family: After reopening, the boardwalk, wetland habitat, wildlife viewing, and waterfall can support a short family nature visit. Children need close supervision on boardwalks and near water.
places.dogs: Pet access should be confirmed after construction because narrow boardwalks, wildlife habitat, events, and updated site rules may affect dogs.
places.picnic: This is primarily a boardwalk and wetland garden, not a general picnic park. Serenity Falls can be reserved for small ceremonies after reopening.
places.landmarks: The main landmarks are the elevated wetland boardwalk and Serenity Falls, a recirculating waterfall used as an event backdrop.
places.closures: The entire Bog Garden is closed for construction until further notice. Treat all normal-hours information as suspended until the City explicitly announces reopening.

places.name: Tanger Family Bicentennial Garden
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1105 Hobbs Road, Greensboro, NC 27410
places.summary: Tanger Family Bicentennial Garden is a free 7.5-acre botanical garden with paved paths, public art, sensory garden, wedding gazebo, Old Mill, restrooms, parking, picnic areas, and connections to David Caldwell Historic Park.
places.hours: The garden opens daily at 8 a.m., weather permitting, and closes at 5 p.m. in winter, 7 p.m. in spring and early fall, and 8 p.m. in summer. It closes Thanksgiving and Christmas.
places.cost: Casual garden access is free. Weddings, reserved spaces, and paid professional photography require current fees or permits.
places.parking: Use 1105 Hobbs Road. Parking is available near the garden and accessible routes; choose the garden side rather than the separately closed Bog Garden across Hobbs Road.
places.restroom: Restrooms are listed as a reasonably accessible garden feature and are convenient to the gazebo and major developed areas.
places.accessibility: Parking, paved walking trail, public garden, restrooms, gazebo, and several event lawns and picnic areas provide reasonably accessible options.
places.trail: Paved garden paths connect botanical displays, public art, sensory garden, Old Mill, gazebo, and David Caldwell Historic Park. This is a garden walk rather than a natural trail system.
places.family: Families can explore the sensory garden, public art, Old Mill, lawns, plants, shaded picnic area, and neighboring historic park. Keep children out of planting beds and water features.
places.dogs: Follow posted garden rules and keep any permitted dog leashed and away from planting beds, ceremonies, and reserved spaces.
places.picnic: The wooded picnic area includes tables and shade, while other lawns and reservable sites have different rules. Reserve space for organized or exclusive use.
places.landmarks: Look for the Chandler Wedding Gazebo, Sensory Garden, Old Mill, public art, Adelman Lawn, wooded picnic area, and David Caldwell Historic Park.
places.closures: Weather, horticultural work, weddings, reservations, holidays, and seasonal closing times can affect access. Bog Garden across the road is separately closed for construction.

places.name: Keeley Park
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: 4100 Keeley Road, McLeansville, NC 27301
places.summary: Keeley Park is a large inclusive recreation park with an all-abilities playground, seasonal sprayground, paved trails, fishing ponds and pier, community garden, picnic shelters, disc golf, pump track, beginner mountain-bike trail, fitness area, and restrooms.
places.hours: The park opens daily at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m. in winter, 7 p.m. in spring and early fall, and 8 p.m. in summer. It closes Thanksgiving and Christmas; the sprayground is seasonal.
places.cost: General park, playground, trails, fishing areas, disc golf, pump track, and fitness access are free. Shelter, sprayground, programs, plots, tournaments, and reservations may use separate rules or fees.
places.parking: Use 4100 Keeley Road for the main park and garden; 4110 Keeley Road is identified for sprayground and disc-golf arrival. Follow signs for the exact activity.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available near the developed accessible recreation area, with facilities near the playground, sprayground, shelters, and pump-track area.
places.accessibility: Accessible features include parking, paved trails, restrooms, shelters, fishing pier, garden, cornhole, outdoor fitness, sprayground, and the Up in the Air all-inclusive playground.
places.trail: Paved walking trails serve the developed park, while the beginner mountain-bike trail and pump track use natural or red-clay surfaces. Do not use the pump track when muddy.
places.family: The all-inclusive playground, seasonal sprayground, fishing ponds, garden, paved trails, fitness equipment, and beginner bike facilities support a broad family visit.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed in ordinary park areas and away from sprayground and playground activity. Follow any posted restrictions on courses, garden plots, and programmed spaces.
places.picnic: Reservable picnic shelters and tables are available. Reserve for organized groups and confirm sprayground or event arrangements separately.
places.landmarks: Major destinations include the Up in the Air playground, sprayground, community garden, fishing ponds, 18-hole disc-golf course, pump track, and beginner mountain-bike trail.
places.closures: Wet conditions can close the red-clay pump track, while weather, maintenance, seasonal sprayground operations, holidays, events, and tournaments can affect individual facilities.

places.name: Atlantic and Yadkin Greenway
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: Old Battleground Road, Greensboro, NC 27410
places.summary: Atlantic and Yadkin Greenway is a major paved north Greensboro trail connecting neighborhoods, Country Park and the Battleground Parks District toward Bur-Mil Park and Summerfield.
places.hours: Use the greenway during posted daylight trail hours. Individual parks, trailheads, and connected facilities use separate schedules.
places.cost: General walking, running, and bicycling access is free. Programs, rentals, parking at adjacent attractions, and connected facilities may charge separately.
places.parking: Choose a mapped trailhead such as Country Park, Lewis Recreation Center, Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, Bur-Mil Park, or another official access point based on the open section.
places.restroom: Restrooms are tied to connected parks and staffed facilities rather than being continuous along the greenway. Plan around a confirmed-open stop.
places.accessibility: The principal greenway is paved, but trailhead design, grades, bridge approaches, detours, and connected natural trails vary. Verify the selected access point.
places.trail: This is a paved multiple-use greenway for walking and bicycling, with connections into the wider Battleground and watershed trail network.
places.family: Families can select a shorter segment near Country Park or another developed trailhead. Teach children to keep right, announce passes, and stop clear of bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use shared greenway sections subject to posted rules. Keep leashes short around bicycles and remove all waste.
places.picnic: Use picnic facilities at connected parks such as Country Park or Bur-Mil rather than blocking the linear trail or trailheads.
places.landmarks: The route connects the Battleground Parks District, Country Park, Guilford Courthouse area, Lake Brandt vicinity, Bur-Mil Park, and northern communities.
places.closures: The northern trestle bridge between Bur-Mil Park and Strawberry Road remains a critical section-specific closure. Check the City greenway page and do not plan a through-route across a posted closure.

places.name: Greensboro Downtown Greenway
places.operator: City of Greensboro Parks and Recreation
places.address: 475 Spring Garden Street, Greensboro, NC 27401
places.summary: Greensboro Downtown Greenway is a completed four-mile paved loop around downtown, featuring public art, landscaped urban spaces, lighting, benches, bicycle racks, drinking fountains, and connections to neighborhoods, universities, parks, and other trails.
places.hours: Use the greenway according to posted trail and park rules. Lighting is present on developed sections, but events, construction, maintenance, and connecting destinations can use separate schedules.
places.cost: General greenway access and public-art viewing are free. Parking, transit, programs, food, and adjacent destinations may charge separately.
places.parking: Official options include street parking near Smith and Prescott, Lindsay and Cumberland, accessible trailhead parking at 475 Spring Garden Street, and trailhead parking at Eugene and Bragg streets.
places.restroom: Restrooms are not continuous around the loop. Plan around a confirmed public facility or open downtown destination rather than assuming every trailhead has one.
places.accessibility: The asphalt and concrete multiple-use route is reasonably accessible by mobility device, and 475 Spring Garden Street provides an accessible trailhead parking option.
places.trail: The completed loop is approximately four miles and typically uses a wide paved urban trail with road crossings, public spaces, lighting, landscaping, and connections.
places.family: Families can choose a short public-art segment or complete the loop. Stay together at road crossings and keep children clear of passing bicycles.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the shared greenway subject to posted rules. Keep the leash short in busy urban sections and remove waste.
places.picnic: Use connected parks or designated public spaces for a stop, without blocking the trail. Organized events and vendors require City approval.
places.landmarks: The loop features public art and four conceptual cornerstones, including accessible Morehead Park parking and connections into downtown neighborhoods and institutions.
places.closures: Events, street work, utility construction, severe weather, maintenance, and temporary detours can affect a section. Check City notices before relying on an exact through-route.

places.name: West Point on the Eno
places.operator: Durham Parks and Recreation
places.address: 5101 North Roxboro Street, Durham, NC 27704. The park has no public vehicle or pedestrian access during the July 2026-January 2027 closure; the Environmental Education Pavilion at 5253 North Roxboro Street remains open.
places.summary: West Point on the Eno is Durham's 404-acre natural and historic Eno River park, normally offering trails, paddling and fishing access, picnic areas, a historic mill, McCown-Mangum House, and Hugh Mangum Museum of Photography. The park is closed July 2026 through January 2027 for accessibility renovations.
places.hours: Closed July 2026 through January 2027 for renovations. Normal gate hours of 8 a.m. to dark are suspended until Durham Parks and Recreation announces reopening.
places.cost: There is normally no general outdoor park admission, but the park is currently closed. Tours, programs, and reservations may use separate registration after reopening.
places.parking: Do not drive to the park entrance during construction; public vehicle and pedestrian access are prohibited. Use only the separately open Environmental Education Pavilion when attending a confirmed program there.
places.restroom: Park restrooms are unavailable during the full closure. The separately operating Environmental Education Pavilion may have facilities only during its own programs and hours.
places.accessibility: The closure supports major ADA upgrades to parking and paths. Do not rely on pre-construction accessibility descriptions; reassess exact routes after the City completes work and publishes reopening guidance.
places.trail: The park normally has wooded and riverside trails across rocky terrain along two miles of the Eno. Every park trail and pedestrian entrance is closed during construction.
places.family: Historic buildings, river scenery, trails, tours, and nature programs normally support family visits. During closure, use only relocated programs at confirmed alternate facilities.
places.dogs: No dog walking is permitted inside the closed park. After reopening, follow posted leash, river, trail, historic-site, and program rules.
places.picnic: Picnic areas are unavailable during construction. Do not plan gatherings or attempt pedestrian entry until reopening is announced.
places.landmarks: Major landmarks are West Point Mill, McCown-Mangum House, Hugh Mangum Museum of Photography, Eno River, and the Environmental Education Pavilion north of the park.
places.closures: The entire park is closed from July 1, 2026 through January 2027 for renovations and ADA upgrades. The historic mill was already closed for building-condition concerns and is not included in this renovation scope.

places.name: Durham Central Park
places.operator: Durham Central Park Inc. in partnership with the City of Durham
places.address: 501 Foster Street, Durham, NC 27701. Use the exact downtown Foster Street destination rather than the unrelated Central Park Drive address elsewhere in Durham.
places.summary: Durham Central Park is a downtown public park with playground, skatepark, restrooms, picnic tables, water fountain, recreation space, field lighting, trail access, events, farmers market, and connections toward the American Tobacco Trail.
places.hours: Outdoor park access follows posted downtown park rules and event conditions. Market, recreation, restroom, sprayground, and programmed spaces use separate schedules.
places.cost: General outdoor park, playground, skatepark, and trail access are free. Markets, vendors, rentals, programs, and ticketed events may charge separately.
places.parking: Use legal downtown street parking or public garages near 501 Foster Street. Market and festival days can close streets and fill the closest spaces, so consider transit or a garage outside the event footprint.
places.restroom: Restrooms and a water fountain are listed park features, but access can vary with maintenance, events, seasonal operations, and current water restrictions.
places.accessibility: The downtown park uses developed paths and public-space connections, but event layouts, street crossings, construction, and individual play or skate features vary. Confirm the best route for the exact activity.
places.trail: Developed paths and greenway access connect park areas and downtown destinations. The nearby American Tobacco Trail provides a longer paved route south from downtown.
places.family: The playground, skatepark, lawns, picnic tables, market activity, and public events make this a flexible family stop. Check age guidance and supervise around skaters, streets, and crowded events.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas subject to posted rules. Markets, food events, playgrounds, skate areas, or crowded programs may impose additional restrictions.
places.picnic: Picnic tables and lawns support casual meals when not reserved or occupied by events. Organized gatherings, vending, and exclusive setups require approval.
places.landmarks: Look for the playground, skatepark, event lawn and pavilion areas, Durham Farmers' Market, Foster Street corridor, and connections toward downtown cultural destinations.
places.closures: Events, markets, street closures, construction, severe weather, and maintenance can alter access. All Durham spraygrounds are currently closed under Stage 2 water restrictions, so do not plan on water play until DPR posts reopening.

places.name: Forest Hills Park
places.operator: Durham Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1639 University Drive, Durham, NC 27707.
places.summary: Forest Hills Park is a 45.86-acre Durham community park with playground, swings, picnic shelter, grills, tennis and pickleball-lined courts, trail access, sprayground, seasonal pool complex, clubhouse, and mature neighborhood landscape.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open dawn to dusk. The pool, sprayground, clubhouse, court reservations, and shelter use separate schedules and current closure notices.
places.cost: General park, playground, courts when unreserved, and trail access are free. Pool admission, rentals, programs, and reservations may charge separately; the pool is currently closed.
places.parking: Use 1639 University Drive and follow internal signs for the playground, courts, pool area, clubhouse, or shelter. Busy programs and court reservations can affect the closest spaces.
places.restroom: Restroom access is associated with developed facilities and their operating conditions. Do not assume pool or clubhouse restrooms are available while those facilities are closed.
places.accessibility: Developed park paths, play areas, courts, and facilities provide practical arrival options, but grades, older infrastructure, event setups, and facility closures can affect exact routes.
places.trail: The park provides greenway or trail access through its rolling neighborhood landscape. Surfaces and grades vary between developed paths, lawn edges, and connections.
places.family: Families normally use the playground, toddler and standard swings, picnic shelter, courts, and sprayground. The sprayground and pool are currently unavailable.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed in ordinary park areas and away from playground and aquatic spaces. Follow posted rules around courts, shelters, programs, and the clubhouse.
places.picnic: A reservable picnic shelter, tables, and grills are available. Reserve for guaranteed group use and confirm water and restroom conditions before an event.
places.landmarks: The park's main destinations are the playground and sprayground area, Forest Hills Pool, historic neighborhood clubhouse, tennis and pickleball courts, and picnic shelter.
places.closures: Forest Hills Pool is closed for the 2026 season. The sprayground is closed under Durham's Stage 2 water restrictions and also has a separate water-leak closure; verify both before expecting water play.

places.name: Rock Quarry Park
places.operator: Durham Parks and Recreation
places.address: 701 Stadium Drive, Durham, NC 27704.
places.summary: Rock Quarry Park is a 46-acre Durham recreation and event campus with Edison Johnson Recreation and Aquatic Centers, playground, sprayground, dog park, athletic field, tennis courts, picnic tables, restrooms, fitness equipment, and connecting trail.
places.hours: Outdoor park and dog-park areas are open dawn to dusk. Recreation, aquatic, event, court, and sprayground facilities use separate schedules.
places.cost: General outdoor park, playground, trail, fitness equipment, and ordinary recreation access are free. Aquatics, rentals, programs, reservations, and major events may charge.
places.parking: Use 701 Stadium Drive or the Edison Johnson facility parking based on your destination. Major festivals need overflow plans and can change internal traffic and parking access.
places.restroom: Restrooms are listed at the park and recreation facilities, but operating access varies. The park water fountain and dog-park water pump are currently shut off for emergency maintenance.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, paved connections, recreation facilities, event space, and play areas provide accessible options. Confirm the route to the dog park, which lies along the Rock Quarry Spur Trail.
places.trail: A short trail connects the recreation and aquatic centers with the large field and tennis courts, and the Rock Quarry Spur Trail reaches the dog park.
places.family: Families can use the playground, swings, fitness area, courts, picnic tables, recreation programs, and aquatic center when open. The sprayground is currently closed under water restrictions.
places.dogs: The registered-dog facility has small, large, and program areas. It closes 7 a.m.-noon on the third Monday monthly for maintenance, and the dog-park water pump is currently unavailable.
places.picnic: Picnic tables and a grill are available, while the event lawn and indoor rooms require reservations. Large events must provide additional off-site parking.
places.landmarks: Major destinations include Edison Johnson Recreation Center, Aquatic Center, Rock Quarry Dog Park, playground and sprayground, event field, tennis courts, and outdoor fitness equipment.
places.closures: All Durham spraygrounds are closed under Stage 2 water restrictions. The park water fountain and dog-park pump are shut off until further notice, and the dog park has a recurring third-Monday maintenance closure.

places.name: Leigh Farm Park
places.operator: Durham Parks and Recreation
places.address: 370 Leigh Farm Road, Durham, NC 27707.
places.summary: Leigh Farm Park is an 82.8-acre natural and historic Durham property with a seven-acre National Register core, 1835 Leigh House, historic outbuildings, visitor center, wooded trails, picnic tables, restrooms, and an 18-hole disc-golf course.
places.hours: Park gates are open daily year-round from 8 a.m. to dark. Public tours are normally offered Saturdays from April through mid-December, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., subject to staffing and events.
places.cost: General park, trail, historic-ground, picnic, and disc-golf access are free. Camps, programs, private tours, tournaments, and reservations may charge or require registration.
places.parking: Use the entrance at 370 Leigh Farm Road. Parking is intentionally limited to protect the historic setting, and visitors should expect a walk from the entrance lot.
places.restroom: Restrooms and a water fountain are listed park features near developed visitor areas. Do not assume facilities are available deep within wooded acreage.
places.accessibility: Limited parking and required walking are important constraints. Historic buildings, older surfaces, wooded trails, and the disc-golf course vary; contact DPR before relying on a specific step-free tour.
places.trail: Wooded park routes connect the historic core and broader property, while the 18-hole disc-golf course crosses recreation terrain. Expect natural surfaces beyond developed visitor areas.
places.family: Families can explore historic grounds, scheduled tours, picnic tables, wooded areas, wildlife programs, and disc golf. Interpret the plantation and enslaved-person history thoughtfully with children.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and away from historic buildings, wildlife programs, camps, and active disc-golf play. Follow posted park and partner-program rules.
places.picnic: Picnic tables support casual visits. Contact DPR for groups, programs, commercial activity, exclusive setups, or gatherings that could affect the historic site.
places.landmarks: The historic core includes Leigh House, dairy, enslaved peoples cabins, smokehouse, corn crib, well house, carriage house, cemetery, tobacco barn, and pack house.
places.closures: Tours, visitor-center access, partner programs, historic interiors, disc-golf events, weather, and preservation work can change independently. Verify a building-specific visit before traveling.

places.name: Lake Michie Park and Marina
places.operator: Durham Parks and Recreation
places.address: 2802 Bahama Road, Bahama, NC 27503. Do not travel to the entrance while the facility remains closed to all activity.
places.summary: Lake Michie Park and Marina is a seasonal northern Durham County fishing and boating facility with picnic tables, restrooms, accessible boathouse, dock, and canoe and kayak launch. It is currently closed to all activity because of unsafe low water levels.
places.hours: Closed to all activity until further notice because of low water. Normal 2026 seasonal hours are suspended; reopening requires an explicit Durham Parks and Recreation update.
places.cost: No activity or admission is currently available. After reopening, fishing, launch, boat, motor, and rental fees apply according to current City resident and nonresident rates.
places.parking: The official entrance is 2802 Bahama Road, but visitors should not travel there during the full closure. Wait for a City lake alert confirming reopening and safe access.
places.restroom: Restrooms and marina facilities are unavailable during the closure. Recheck operating days and hours after reopening.
places.accessibility: The normal facility includes an ADA-accessible boathouse, dock, and canoe or kayak launch. Low water makes all activity unsafe, so those features are currently unavailable.
places.trail: Lake Michie is a water-access and fishing destination rather than a trail park. Shore, dock, ramp, and launch conditions depend directly on water level and operations.
places.family: Fishing, picnicking, and boating can support family visits when the lake is safely open. At present, no family or recreational activity is permitted.
places.dogs: Do not bring a dog to the closed facility. After reopening, follow marina, dock, water-supply, leash, and boat rules.
places.picnic: Picnic tables normally support simple lake visits, but all picnic and shoreline use is prohibited during the full closure.
places.landmarks: Visitor facilities normally include the marina, boathouse, fishing dock, boat launch, and canoe and kayak access on Lake Michie.
places.closures: Lake Michie Park and Marina has been closed to all activity since June 5, 2026 due to low water levels and will remain closed until the City determines conditions are safe.

places.name: American Tobacco Trail
places.operator: Durham Parks and Recreation and regional trail partners
places.address: For the Durham downtown end, begin near Morehead and Blackwell streets. Choose a specific park or official access address for other sections rather than navigating to a generic midpoint.
places.summary: The Durham section of the American Tobacco Trail is an 11-mile, ten-foot-wide paved rail trail running from downtown near Morehead and Blackwell streets to the Chatham County line toward Jordan Lake, used by walkers, runners, cyclists, skaters, strollers, and mobility devices.
places.hours: Use the trail according to posted daylight and park rules. Connected parks, restrooms, events, maintenance projects, and neighboring jurisdictions can use separate schedules.
places.cost: General trail access is free. Parking, transit, programs, food, rentals, and adjacent destinations may charge separately.
places.parking: Choose a destination-specific access point. Downtown users can begin near Morehead and Blackwell; Elmira Avenue Park, Solite Park, and C.M. Herndon Park provide useful developed stops along the Durham section.
places.restroom: Durham identifies restrooms at Elmira Park, Solite Park, and C.M. Herndon Park. They are not continuous along the 11-mile route, so plan stops before a long trip.
places.accessibility: The Durham section is a ten-foot-wide paved off-road trail suitable for many mobility devices, but street crossings, grades, trailheads, detours, and restroom approaches vary.
places.trail: The Durham section is 11 miles of paved off-road former rail corridor. Users should keep speeds below 10 mph, watch for other users, and use care at street-level crossings and spurs.
places.family: Families can choose a short out-and-back from a park with restrooms or travel a longer section with bicycles and strollers. Teach children to keep right and stop clear of through traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the shared trail subject to posted rules. Keep leashes short around bicycles, runners, skaters, wildlife, and road crossings, and remove waste.
places.picnic: Use picnic facilities at connected parks rather than stopping in the travel lane. Organized events, vendors, and group setups require permission from the relevant jurisdiction.
places.landmarks: The trail links downtown Durham, neighborhoods and parks, historic rail-corridor landscapes, the Riddle Road Spur, the Chatham County line, and the larger route toward Jordan Lake.
places.closures: Storm damage, bridge or pavement work, street projects, vegetation management, flooding, and jurisdiction-specific maintenance can create detours. Check Durham trail notices before a long through-trip.

places.name: Salem Lake Park
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: 815 Salem Lake Road, Winston-Salem, NC 27107. Use the main or Point lot for the playground, picnic areas, marina, and primary trail access; Linville Road provides another trail access point.
places.summary: Salem Lake Park centers on a 365-acre lake with a mostly natural-surface seven-mile loop trail, fishing pier, marina, playground, picnic areas, restrooms, concessions, and a connection to Salem Creek Greenway.
places.hours: The park is open sunrise to sunset, but lake and trail users must exit 30 minutes before closing. Current marina and gate hours are 8 a.m.-7 p.m. weekdays and 7 a.m.-7 p.m. weekends, with lake and pier access ending at 6:30 p.m.; seasonal times can change.
places.cost: General park, playground, picnic, and trail access are free. Pier fishing and boat launching have posted fees, and anglers age 16 or older need a North Carolina fishing license.
places.parking: For the marina, playground, picnic areas, and mile-zero Point access, use 815 Salem Lake Road. Trail users can also use the Linville Road area; trail parking may be outside the main gates when marina gates are closed.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at the marina office, near the playground and picnic area, and at the Linville Road access. Facilities are not continuous around the seven-mile loop.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, marina, pier, playground, picnic, and restroom areas offer practical access, but most of the lake loop is dirt with changing grades, weather effects, and equestrian traffic.
places.trail: The lake loop is seven miles and eight feet wide, with some pavement but mostly dirt. Mile markers run counterclockwise from the Point lot; walkers, runners, cyclists, and equestrians share the route.
places.family: Families can combine the playground, picnic areas, lake views, short trail segments, and fishing. A full loop is a substantial outing, so carry water and plan restroom stops.
places.dogs: Dogs must be leashed, waste removed, and pets kept under control around horses, bicycles, wildlife, the pier, playground, and shared paths.
places.picnic: The shelter and pavilion are shared public spaces and are not reservable for exclusive use. Small groups may use them without blocking other visitors or setting up across large areas.
places.landmarks: Key destinations are the marina center, fishing pier, Point playground and picnic area, seven-mile Salem Lake Trail, Linville Road access, dam area, and Salem Creek Greenway connection.
places.closures: Storm damage, high water, maintenance, marina operations, and seasonal closing times can affect the trail or lake. Call the marina for current trail conditions before a full loop; the lake and trail close before the outer gate.

places.name: The Quarry at Grant Park
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: 1790 Quarry Road, Winston-Salem, NC 27107. Enter from Reynolds Park Road beside William R. Anderson Recreation Center rather than approaching the quarry rim from an unmapped side.
places.summary: The Quarry at Grant Park is a 200-acre scenic park built around a former stone quarry, with a dramatic overlook pier, skyline views, amphitheater, open lawn, restrooms, drinking fountains, walking paths, and greenway access.
places.hours: The park is open sunrise to sunset. Leave enough time to return from overlooks and trails before dark, and follow posted gate or event times.
places.cost: General park, overlook, lawn, and trail access are free. Reserved events, programs, and nearby recreation facilities may have separate fees.
places.parking: Use the signed entrance from Reynolds Park Road and the park lot near William R. Anderson Recreation Center. The Waughtown Connector also provides pedestrian and bicycle access.
places.restroom: Restrooms and drinking fountains are listed park features near the developed arrival and amphitheater area; do not assume facilities are available at every overlook.
places.accessibility: The developed entrance, broad paths, overlook areas, amphitheater, lawn, and restrooms provide accessible options, though grades and exact overlook approaches vary.
places.trail: Developed walking paths connect the main overlook pier, secondary viewpoints, lawn, and greenway access. Stay on designated routes and behind barriers around the steep quarry rim.
places.family: The skyline and quarry views, lawn, amphitheater, and manageable walking routes work for a scenic family stop. Closely supervise children because the water and cliffs are not recreation areas.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under posted park rules. Keep them behind barriers, away from cliff edges and wildlife, and remove waste.
places.picnic: The open lawn can support a simple visit, but the park does not list picnic shelters or grills. Organized gatherings and amphitheater use require City approval.
places.landmarks: The signature landmark is the overlook pier extending toward the flooded quarry, with additional overlooks, amphitheater, skyline view, and Waughtown Connector access.
places.closures: Severe weather, ice, maintenance, events, or unsafe overlook conditions can restrict access. Swimming, diving, fishing, boating, kayaking, and entering the quarry water are prohibited.

places.name: Hanes Park
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: 1406 Northwest Boulevard, Winston-Salem, NC 27104. The park borders Reynolds High School, Wiley Middle School, the Central YMCA, and West End neighborhood streets.
places.summary: Hanes Park is a historic 47-acre recreation park with a playground, 1.1-mile track, tennis complex, ball fields, open play areas, picnic shelters, restrooms, and prominent stone entrances.
places.hours: The park is open sunrise to sunset. Courts, fields, school activities, programs, and construction areas use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, track when open, and casual recreation access are free. Court programs, leagues, field reservations, and organized activities may charge or reserve space.
places.parking: Use 1406 Northwest Boulevard and legal park or neighborhood parking. School events, tournaments, YMCA activity, and construction can fill the closest spaces.
places.restroom: Restrooms and drinking fountains are listed park features, but access may vary with maintenance, field activity, and construction.
places.accessibility: Renovated entrances, paths, seating walls, lighting, parking, and developed recreation areas improve access, but slopes and construction detours can change the best route.
places.trail: The park's running and walking track is about 1.1 miles. Beginning August 3, 2026, the track closes for resurfacing and drainage repairs; other park routes are not equivalent substitutes.
places.family: Families can use the playground, open areas, picnic shelters, ball fields, and courts when available. Expect school and tournament traffic at peak times.
places.dogs: Dogs must be leashed outside any specifically designated dog facility; Hanes Park does not list an off-leash dog park. Keep pets off active courts and fields.
places.picnic: Picnic shelters and open areas support casual visits. Reserve fields or organized activities through the City rather than assuming exclusive use.
places.landmarks: Look for the semicircular stone entrance, historic track and field layout, Joe White Tennis Center area, playground, ball fields, and West End neighborhood edge.
places.closures: The running track is scheduled to close beginning August 3, 2026 for resurfacing and repair. Construction, school events, tournaments, drainage work, and field reservations can affect other areas.

places.name: Washington Park
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: 1490 South Broad Street, Winston-Salem, NC 27127. This entrance serves the main recreation park, with connections to Salem Creek Greenway and Gateway Nature Preserve.
places.summary: Washington Park is a large urban recreation park with playground, dog park, amphitheater, ball field, basketball, fitness course, picnic shelters, restrooms, walking loops, Salem Creek Greenway access, and neighboring Gateway Nature Preserve.
places.hours: Follow posted City park hours; the facility page and citywide guidance may express closing as sunrise-to-sunset or posted evening hours. Greenway, reserved fields, dog park, events, and restrooms can operate differently.
places.cost: General park, playground, dog park, fitness, walking, and greenway access are free. Reservations, leagues, programs, and organized events may charge.
places.parking: Use 1490 South Broad Street for the main park. Choose a legal trailhead or connected destination for longer Salem Creek Greenway trips rather than leaving a vehicle after park closing.
places.restroom: Restrooms and drinking fountains are listed near developed park facilities. The greenway and nature preserve do not provide continuous restroom access.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, paths, shelters, playground, fitness, and restroom areas provide accessible choices, while natural habitat trails, grades, and older connections vary.
places.trail: The park has half-mile and one-mile walking routes plus a 1.11-mile fitness course. The connected Salem Creek Greenway is an eight-foot paved route extending 5.2 miles toward Old Salem and Salem Lake.
places.family: The playground, fields, basketball, fitness stations, picnic shelters, greenway, and neighboring nature preserve offer several family visit styles in one area.
places.dogs: Washington Park includes the City's designated off-leash dog park. Dogs must be leashed elsewhere in the park and greenway, and owners must remove waste.
places.picnic: Picnic shelters, grills, electrical outlets, and open areas support meals and groups. Reserve a shelter or stage for guaranteed organized use.
places.landmarks: Key areas include the playground, dog park, amphitheater, fitness course, Salem Creek Greenway, and the adjacent 19-acre Gateway Nature Preserve and pollinator garden.
places.closures: Flooding along Salem Creek, greenway work, events, field reservations, weather, and maintenance can alter access. Confirm trail detours before using Washington Park as a through-trip trailhead.

places.name: Tanglewood Park
places.operator: Forsyth County Parks and Recreation
places.address: 4061 Clemmons Road, Clemmons, NC 27012. Enter through the main entrance from US 158; GPS can incorrectly route visitors to an inaccessible rear side of the park.
places.summary: Tanglewood Park is a major Forsyth County destination with trails, two year-round playgrounds, picnic areas, arboretum and rose garden, dog park, golf, tennis, stables, aquatics, campground, Mallard Lake, historic areas, and seasonal events.
places.hours: General day-use areas are open sunrise to sunset unless posted otherwise; the playgrounds are open daily 7 a.m. to dusk. Golf, tennis, stables, pool, campground, offices, rentals, and events use separate schedules.
places.cost: Current vehicle entrance is $2 for personal vehicles and $8 for passenger vans and buses. Golf, aquatics, camping, stables, rentals, programs, and events have additional fees; motorcycles are prohibited.
places.parking: Use the US 158 main entrance at 4061 Clemmons Road and follow internal signs for the exact feature. Do not follow GPS directions to the inaccessible rear boundary.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are available at both playground areas and other developed facilities. Hours vary around golf, aquatics, camping, rentals, and seasonal operations.
places.accessibility: The park provides developed roads, parking, paved routes, playground and picnic facilities, but its large footprint, historic areas, natural trails, stable terrain, and individual attractions vary.
places.trail: Tanglewood includes paved and natural routes plus designated bridle trails. Class 1 and 2 e-bikes are allowed only on paved trails, and horses are limited to marked bridle routes.
places.family: Two year-round playgrounds near Shelter 4 and Mallard Lake, public picnic areas, gardens, trails, seasonal aquatics, horses, and events make this a multi-destination family park.
places.dogs: Use Tanglewoof Dog Park only when its status line confirms it is open. Dogs elsewhere must follow leash rules; maintenance can temporarily close the off-leash area.
places.picnic: Public picnic areas and restrooms sit beside both playgrounds, and reservable shelters support groups. The playgrounds themselves remain public and cannot be reserved exclusively.
places.landmarks: Major destinations include Mallard Lake, Shelter 4 playground, Tanglewoof Dog Park, Arboretum and Rose Garden, golf courses, stables, aquatics center, campground, and historic estate landscape.
places.closures: Weather, maintenance, Festival of Lights traffic, tournaments, dog-park work, and seasonal facilities can change access. Check the exact attraction and dog-park status before traveling.

places.name: Winston Lake Park
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: 1344 Winston Park Drive, Winston-Salem, NC 27101. Follow internal signs for the lake trail, playgrounds, picnic shelters, golf course, pool, splash pad, or athletic areas.
places.summary: Winston Lake Park is a large lakefront recreation campus with a 2.4-mile shoreline trail, multiple playgrounds, picnic shelters, restrooms, seasonal pool and splash pad, ball field, golf course, horseshoes, concessions, and open play areas.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open sunrise to sunset. Pool, splash pad, concessions, golf, fields, and reserved facilities use separate seasonal or programmed schedules.
places.cost: General outdoor park, playground, picnic, and walking-trail access are free. Golf, pool, programs, concessions, leagues, and reservations may charge.
places.parking: Use 1344 Winston Park Drive and choose the lot nearest your activity. Golf, aquatic, league, and event traffic can make one area busy while another remains accessible.
places.restroom: Restrooms and drinking fountains are listed at the developed park. Aquatic, golf, and concession facilities may not be open whenever the outdoor park is open.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, playground, shelter, restroom, and recreation areas offer accessible options, but shoreline trail surfaces, grades, and attraction-specific access vary.
places.trail: The shoreline walking trail is about 2.4 miles. Confirm current surface and weather conditions before relying on the entire loop with a stroller or mobility device.
places.family: Multiple playgrounds, lake views, shelters, open play, seasonal swimming and splash pad, and a manageable shoreline trail support varied family visits.
places.dogs: Dogs must be leashed and kept out of restricted aquatic, playground, golf, and athletic areas. Remove waste and yield on the shoreline trail.
places.picnic: Picnic shelters, grills, electrical outlets, and open areas support meals. Reserve shelters or fields for organized groups and confirm nearby restroom availability.
places.landmarks: The principal areas are Winston Lake and shoreline trail, three playground locations, golf course, seasonal pool and splash pad, ball field, and picnic shelters.
places.closures: Aquatic features are seasonal, while weather, lake conditions, golf operations, field reservations, maintenance, and events can affect specific facilities without closing the entire park.

places.name: Muddy Creek Greenway
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: For developed access, use Jamison Park near 285 Meadowlark Drive, Winston-Salem, NC 27106. The greenway also connects Country Club Road, Robinhood Road, schools, neighborhoods, and the Summerfield bridge.
places.summary: Muddy Creek Greenway is a 2.9-mile, ten-foot-wide paved shared-use trail running from Country Club Road through Jamison Park and under Robinhood Road toward the Summerfield neighborhood and Jefferson Elementary School.
places.hours: Use the greenway during posted daylight park hours. Connected parks, school areas, neighborhood connectors, construction zones, and parking lots may use separate restrictions.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Programs, nearby facilities, and private parking are separate; use public access points rather than business lots.
places.parking: Jamison Park provides the clearest developed trailhead with parking and facilities. Other connections are neighborhood or school access points and should not be assumed to provide public parking.
places.restroom: Plan on developed facilities at Jamison Park rather than continuous restrooms along the 2.9-mile corridor. Availability can vary seasonally and with maintenance.
places.accessibility: The ten-foot paved trail supports many wheelchairs, mobility devices, and strollers, but grades, bridge approaches, street crossings, temporary repairs, and connector paths vary.
places.trail: The completed greenway is about 2.9 miles of ten-foot pavement along Muddy Creek, passing under Robinhood Road and connecting five neighborhood routes, Jamison Park, and nearby schools.
places.family: A short out-and-back from Jamison Park combines a playground and developed facilities with the paved greenway. Teach children to keep right and stop clear of faster users.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed under City greenway rules. Keep leashes short around bicycles and other users, and remove waste.
places.picnic: Use Jamison Park for picnic and gathering space rather than blocking the greenway. Organized trail events require City approval.
places.landmarks: Connections include Jamison Park, Country Club Road, Robinhood Road, Jefferson Elementary, Meadowlark schools, Cedar Trail, Century Oaks, Lantern Ridge, Stonebridge, Summerfield, and Brooks Landing.
places.closures: Flooding, creek erosion, bridge work, utility projects, and pavement repairs can close or detour sections. Check City greenway notices before depending on it as a continuous route.

places.name: J. Bayard Clark Park and Nature Center
places.operator: Fayetteville-Cumberland Parks and Recreation
places.address: 631 Sherman Drive, Fayetteville, NC 28301. Use this entrance for the nature center and wooded trails; the nearby Moses Mathis Bicycle Man trailhead serves the Cape Fear River Trail.
places.summary: Clark Park is a wooded nature and education destination with live-animal exhibits, unpaved trails, picnic areas, StoryWalk, a coastal-plain waterfall overlook, restrooms, playground access, and a central Cape Fear River Trail trailhead.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open daily 8 a.m. to dusk. The Nature Center is generally open Monday-Friday 10 a.m.-4 p.m. and Saturdays March-October 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; confirm holiday and program changes.
places.cost: General park, nature-center, trail, playground, StoryWalk, and picnic access are free. Some registered programs, group services, or rentals use separate arrangements.
places.parking: Use 631 Sherman Drive for Clark Park and the nature center. This is also one of the primary parking locations for the Cape Fear River Trail, so spaces can be busier on pleasant weekends.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available in the developed park and nature-center area. Do not expect facilities along every wooded path or between distant Cape Fear River Trail access points.
places.accessibility: The developed parking, nature center, playground and restroom area provides the most practical access. Unpaved woodland trails, slopes, waterfall approaches and remote routes vary.
places.trail: Clark Park has its own unpaved woodland trails and connects to the ten-foot paved Cape Fear River Trail. The separate mountain-bike network begins about one mile north along the river trail near Eastwood Avenue.
places.family: Families can combine live-animal exhibits, StoryWalk, the Moses Mathis playground, picnic views, short woodland routes, and a manageable out-and-back on the paved river trail.
places.dogs: Well-behaved dogs are welcome on trails when leashed. Remove waste and keep pets controlled around wildlife, live animals, children, bicycles, and indoor nature-center spaces.
places.picnic: Picnic areas overlook the woods and waterfall setting. Contact the park for school groups, ranger programs, reserved use, or visits that need guaranteed facilities.
places.landmarks: Look for the Nature Center, live-animal displays, StoryWalk, waterfall overlook, Moses Mathis Bicycle Man playground and trailhead, wooded paths, and Cape Fear River Trail connection.
places.closures: Severe weather, high water, fallen trees, trail work, programs, holidays, and building staffing can affect individual features. The outdoor park may remain open when the Nature Center is closed.

places.name: Cape Fear River Trail
places.operator: Fayetteville-Cumberland Parks and Recreation
places.address: For central access use Clark Park near 511-631 Sherman Drive, Fayetteville, NC 28301. Jordan Soccer Complex and Riverside Dog Park provide other access points with different parking capacity.
places.summary: The Cape Fear River Trail is a paved, ten-foot-wide shared route extending more than seven miles one way between Jordan Soccer Complex and the Cross Creek trail connection, with river views, bridges, wetland boardwalks, wildlife signs, and mountain-bike access.
places.hours: The trail is open 365 days a year from 8 a.m. to dusk. Connected parks, restrooms, dog park, soccer complex, and construction areas may use different schedules.
places.cost: General trail access is free. Programs, events, rentals, and nearby facilities may charge separately.
places.parking: Primary parking is available at Jordan Soccer Complex and Clark Park; Riverside Dog Park has limited parking. The trail is not a loop, so long one-way trips require a return plan or pickup.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at developed park and trailhead locations such as Clark Park, but not continuously across the route. Plan stops before a long trip.
places.accessibility: The main trail is ten feet wide and paved with long boardwalk and bridge sections, but some hills are steep and approaches, temporary detours, and connecting paths vary.
places.trail: The route is more than seven miles one way, with flat and hilly pavement, wooden bridges, a covered bridge, and over 1,000 feet of wetland boardwalk. Cyclists must stay under 15 mph and yield to pedestrians.
places.family: Choose a short out-and-back from Clark Park or another developed trailhead rather than attempting the full one-way distance without transportation. Bring water and supervise at slopes and road connections.
places.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed and owners must remove waste. Keep leashes short around bicycles, runners, boardwalks, wildlife, and narrow or steep sections.
places.picnic: Use picnic facilities at Clark Park or another connected park rather than stopping across the shared travel lane. Organized trail events require approval.
places.landmarks: Highlights include Clark Park and the Moses Mathis trailhead, river overlooks, covered bridge, wetland boardwalks, Jordan Soccer Complex, mountain-bike access, Riverside Dog Park connector, and East Coast Greenway designation.
places.closures: Flooding, storm debris, bridge or boardwalk work, river conditions, and construction can interrupt sections. Check City notices before relying on a continuous seven-mile trip.

places.name: Lake Rim Park
places.operator: Fayetteville-Cumberland Parks and Recreation
places.address: 2214 Tar Kiln Drive, Fayetteville, NC 28304. This is the regional park and ranger-office destination, separate from Lake Rim Recreation Center and Lake Rim Aquatic Center addresses.
places.summary: Lake Rim Park is a regional family recreation and nature park with playgrounds, picnic shelters, athletic fields, tennis, sand volleyball, restrooms, StoryWalk, natural areas, and a one-mile border trail through wetlands toward Bones Creek.
places.hours: Park hours are 7 a.m.-9 p.m. March-October and 7 a.m.-5 p.m. November-February. The office is generally open Monday-Friday 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; programs and nearby aquatics use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, StoryWalk, courts and fields when unreserved are free. Shelter and field reservations, outreach programs, and separate aquatic facilities may charge.
places.parking: Use 2214 Tar Kiln Drive for Lake Rim Park. Do not navigate to the recreation center on Hoke Loop Road or aquatic center when your destination is the park trail, playgrounds, or ranger office.
places.restroom: Restrooms are listed park features near developed recreation and shelter areas. They are not continuous along the wetland border trail.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, playground, shelter, court, field and restroom areas provide practical options, while wetland paths, natural surfaces and the Bones Creek route vary.
places.trail: The signature border trail is about one mile through wetlands toward Bones Creek. The park also has developed walking connections among fields, playgrounds, courts and picnic areas.
places.family: Multiple playgrounds, StoryWalk, monthly scavenger activities, sports areas, picnic shelters and a short nature trail support both active and low-key family visits.
places.dogs: Leashed, well-behaved dogs are welcome when kept under control. Remove waste and keep pets away from playground activity, reserved fields, programs and sensitive wetland habitat.
places.picnic: Picnic shelters and areas are first come, first served unless reserved. Reserve through the park office for guaranteed group use.
places.landmarks: Key areas include the playgrounds, StoryWalk, one-mile wetland border trail, Bones Creek direction, picnic shelters, athletic fields, tennis courts and ranger office.
places.closures: Heavy rain, wetland flooding, field conditions, reservations, maintenance and seasonal closing times can affect parts of the park. Aquatic and recreation-center notices do not necessarily apply to this separate property.

places.name: Festival Park
places.operator: Fayetteville-Cumberland Parks and Recreation
places.address: 225 Ray Avenue, Fayetteville, NC 28301, at Ray Avenue and Rowan Street. Event entrances, street closures, security screening, and parking routes can change by program.
places.summary: Festival Park is a 14-acre downtown event park with a large performance stage, lawn seating, vendor promenade, pedestrian paths, creek-trail connection, concessions support, dressing rooms, and public restrooms.
places.hours: Casual access follows posted park conditions, but event gates and closing times control during concerts and festivals. Confirm the specific event schedule before traveling.
places.cost: Ordinary public park access is free. Events may be free or ticketed, and parking, concessions, rentals, or special programs may charge.
places.parking: Use legal downtown street parking, City lots, or the Hay and Franklin Street decks. Weekday parking is enforced, and large events can close the Festival Park Plaza lot and nearby streets or use event pricing.
places.restroom: Public restrooms support the venue, but availability can depend on events, staffing, maintenance, and park setup. Do not assume backstage or concession facilities are publicly accessible.
places.accessibility: The broad promenade, lawn perimeter, downtown sidewalks, venue support areas and nearby ADA parking offer developed access, but crowd barriers, grass seating, security lines and closures vary by event.
places.trail: Pedestrian walkways cross the park and connect toward the creek trail and downtown network. This is primarily an event lawn rather than a long trail destination.
places.family: The open lawn works for casual visits when no setup is underway, while festivals and concerts can be strong family destinations. Review noise, crowd, bag, chair, weather and age guidance for each event.
places.dogs: Pet access can be restricted during concerts, food events, fireworks, security screening or large crowds. Check the event rules rather than relying on ordinary park expectations.
places.picnic: Casual use depends on event setup. Outside food, coolers, chairs, tents and large setups can be limited; organized use and exclusive access require a rental.
places.landmarks: The defining areas are the 40-by-66-foot main stage, grass audience lawn, patterned vendor promenade, backstage and concession support, public restrooms, and creek-trail connection.
places.closures: Festivals, concerts, fireworks, private rentals, load-in, security screening and downtown street closures can take over the park. Event clear-bag and cooler rules may apply even when general park rules are broader.

places.name: Mazarick Park
places.operator: Fayetteville-Cumberland Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1400 Belvedere Avenue, Fayetteville, NC 28301 for the main park side; 1612 Belvedere Avenue serves the opposite side. Follow signs for playgrounds, shelters, Glenville Lake, disc golf, or The Courts at Glenville Lake.
places.summary: Mazarick Park is a regional recreation park around Glenville Lake with playgrounds, three picnic shelters, a paved mile-long loop, shorter natural trail, fishing pier, disc golf, ball field, and the new Courts at Glenville Lake tennis and pickleball complex.
places.hours: The park is open 8 a.m. to dusk. Tennis facilities, programs, building rentals, fields and reserved shelters can use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, trails, disc golf and pier access are free. Fishing-license requirements, court programs, rentals, events and reservations are separate.
places.parking: Use 1400 Belvedere Avenue for one side or 1612 Belvedere Avenue for the other, based on the mapped feature. The new tennis complex and events can shift which lot is most convenient.
places.restroom: Restrooms are shown near developed playground, shelter and recreation areas on both sides of the park. Availability can vary with operations and maintenance.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, paved trail, playground and shelter areas offer accessible choices, but natural trail, disc-golf terrain, lake edge and older connections vary.
places.trail: The park map shows roughly 1.04 miles of paved multi-purpose trail plus about 0.3 miles of unpaved trail, with bridges and connections among both park sides.
places.family: Families can combine playgrounds, paved walking, shelters, disc golf, lake views, fishing pier and nearby courts. Closely supervise children around Glenville Lake.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled around playgrounds, courts, disc golfers, trails and the lake. Remove waste and follow posted restrictions for programmed facilities.
places.picnic: Three shelters and public picnic areas are available first come, first served unless reserved. Shelter and building rentals are handled through different City contacts.
places.landmarks: Major destinations include Glenville Lake and fishing pier, three shelters, playgrounds, Glenville Pines disc-golf course, paved loop, ball field and The Courts at Glenville Lake.
places.closures: Fishing is allowed only from the pier; shoreline fishing, swimming, boats and watercraft are prohibited because Glenville Lake is a water-supply watershed. Weather, court events and maintenance can affect other areas.

places.name: Fred G. Bond Metro Park
places.operator: Town of Cary
places.address: 801 High House Road, Cary, NC 27513 is the main park address. Use 197 Bond Park Drive for the boathouse and waterfront; choose the exact entrance for the community center, senior center, fields, shelters, or challenge course.
places.summary: Fred G. Bond Metro Park is Cary's 310-acre flagship recreation park with Bond Lake, seasonal boathouse rentals, Lazy Daze Playground, fields, picnic shelters, amphitheater, community and senior centers, challenge course, orienteering, and major greenway connections.
places.hours: Park gates open by 7:30 a.m. and close at sunset. The boathouse, community center, senior center, challenge course, amphitheater, programs, and rentals use separate seasonal schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, trails, family picnic areas, and ordinary lakefront access are free. Boat rentals, programs, challenge course, events, shelters, and reserved facilities may charge.
places.parking: Use 801 High House Road for the general park or the destination-specific address. Boathouse parking serves the lake and greenway hub, but event notices can reserve lots and Sertoma guests should not use boathouse spaces except for accessible parking.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available near the boathouse, Kiwanis shelter, community center, playground, and developed facilities. They are not continuous around every trail or lake section.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, community facilities, waterfront deck, boathouse area, playground, shelters, amphitheater approach, and paved trails offer accessible choices, while natural routes and individual activities vary.
places.trail: Bond Park is a major hub for the paved Black Creek and White Oak Creek greenways, Bond Lake Trail, Pine Cone Trail, Paw Paw Trail, Tree ID Trail, and orienteering routes. Surfaces and grades differ outside the main greenways.
places.family: Families can combine Lazy Daze Playground, lakefront picnics, trails, seasonal paddling, fields, nature learning, events, and short walks without needing to use every part of the large park.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled in ordinary park and greenway areas. Dogs are not permitted in boats or restricted play, food, program, and facility areas unless posted otherwise.
places.picnic: Waterfront and deck tables are walk-up spaces for groups of ten or fewer and cannot be reserved for gatherings. Reserve Kiwanis, Buehler, or another designated shelter for an organized group.
places.landmarks: Key destinations include Bond Lake and Boathouse, Lazy Daze Playground, Sertoma Amphitheatre, Kiwanis and Buehler shelters, Challenge Course, Community Center, Senior Center, fields, and Black Creek-White Oak greenway hub.
places.closures: Gate hours, dam work, weather, lake conditions, boat season, events, construction, and reservations can affect separate park areas. Check the exact facility rather than assuming the entire 310-acre park shares one status.

places.name: Hemlock Bluffs Nature Preserve
places.operator: Town of Cary in partnership with North Carolina State Parks
places.address: 2616 Kildaire Farm Road, Cary, NC 27518. Use the Stevens Nature Center entrance for exhibits, restrooms, trail information, and the primary trail network.
places.summary: Hemlock Bluffs is a protected natural area known for rare Eastern hemlocks and mountain plant communities, with Stevens Nature Center, approximately three miles of mulch and natural-surface trails, boardwalks, overlooks, wildlife viewing, and a children's nature trail.
places.hours: The preserve is open daily 9 a.m. until sunset, with gates currently closing at 8:30 p.m. Stevens Nature Center is open Monday-Saturday 10 a.m.-5 p.m. and Sunday 1-5 p.m.
places.cost: General preserve, trail, overlook, children's trail, and exhibit access are free. Registered programs, classes, and group activities may use separate fees or reservations.
places.parking: Use 2616 Kildaire Farm Road and arrive before the posted gate closing. Parking can fill during pleasant weekends and programs; do not leave a vehicle after the preserve gate closes.
places.restroom: Restrooms are currently open at the developed nature-center area. There are no continuous restroom facilities throughout the forest trail network.
places.accessibility: The nature center and developed visitor area provide accessible options, but most preserve trails have mulch or natural surfaces, uneven terrain, slopes, boardwalks, and stairs. Contact staff for a route matched to mobility needs.
places.trail: The preserve has about three miles of trails. Swift Creek Loop is 0.8 mile with roughly 100 stairs each way; Chestnut Oak Loop is 1.2 miles with uneven mild inclines; Beech Tree Cove and hemlock overlooks include optional stairs and steeper returns.
places.family: Stevens Nature Center exhibits and the children's nature trail can support a shorter visit, while older children may enjoy a carefully chosen forest loop. Stay together and on marked trails.
places.dogs: Pets must remain on a leash no longer than six feet, stay on trail, and have waste removed. Wildlife protection and narrow routes make close control important.
places.picnic: Picnicking is discouraged because this is a nature preserve rather than a recreation park. Use designated visitor areas without disturbing plants, wildlife, trails, or programs.
places.landmarks: Look for Stevens Nature Center, Children's Nature Trail, East and West Bluffs, Swift Creek, Eastern hemlock stands, boardwalks, and the West Hemlock, Beech Tree Cove, and creek overlooks.
places.closures: Swift Creek Trail is currently closed because of a fallen tree. Trail rehabilitation, storms, flooding, heat, damaged structures, and gate conditions can close individual routes while the nature center remains open.

places.name: Jack Smith Park
places.operator: Town of Cary
places.address: 9725 Penny Road, Cary, NC 27518, near Holly Springs Road. Follow internal signs for the playground and sprayground, dog park, climbing boulder, shelter, restrooms, or greenway.
places.summary: Jack Smith Park is a 50-acre family recreation destination with a seven-feature seasonal sprayground, playground for ages 2-12, pass-controlled two-acre dog park, ten-foot climbing boulder, shelter, greenway trails, restrooms, open lawn, and farm-inspired public art.
places.hours: The general park is open sunrise to sunset. The dog park is open 7 a.m.-10 p.m. with no entry after 9 p.m.; the sprayground operates seasonally, currently daily 9 a.m.-8 p.m. through September 21, weather permitting.
places.cost: General park, playground, sprayground, boulder, lawn, trails, art, and ordinary picnic access are free. The off-leash dog park requires an annual membership or day pass and signed waiver.
places.parking: Use the park lot at 9725 Penny Road. Parking is limited relative to popular warm-weather demand, so sprayground weekends, events, and shelter use can fill the closest spaces.
places.restroom: Restrooms are currently listed as open near the developed family recreation area. Availability can change with maintenance, weather, or utility problems.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, paved connections, playground, sprayground, shelter, restroom, public art, and open areas provide accessible choices, while the climbing boulder and some greenway surfaces require individual assessment.
places.trail: Paved and unpaved greenway routes connect the park's developed areas and surrounding network. Keep wheeled recreation out of the sprayground and yield on shared paths.
places.family: The playground, free seasonal sprayground, climbing boulder, open lawn, farm-inspired sheep sculptures and whirligigs, picnic area, and trails support a full family outing.
places.dogs: The dog park requires a Cary pass and waiver; children under 12 are not allowed inside. Dogs must be leashed outside the fenced area, and the dog park closes the second Wednesday monthly from 7 a.m. to noon.
places.picnic: Tables and a shelter are available, with shelter reservations accepted October-April. Food, drinks, glass, and pets are prohibited inside the sprayground.
places.landmarks: Major features are Cary's first sprayground, two-acre dog park, ten-foot climbing boulder, age 2-12 playground, Vollis Simpson whirligigs, William Moore sheep sculptures, shelter, and greenway.
places.closures: The sprayground is weather dependent and closes for monthly maintenance, including August 10, with the season ending September 21. The dog park closes the second Wednesday monthly from 7 a.m. to noon.

places.name: Marla Dorrel Park
places.operator: Town of Cary
