places.address: 111 Thurston Drive, Cary, NC 27518. The entire park is closed through August 7, 2026 for repaving; do not travel for playground or misting-garden access until Cary posts reopening.
places.summary: Marla Dorrel Park is home to Kids Together Playground, an inclusive multi-sensory play environment with the Katal dragon climber, basketball and multi-use slabs, pop-up skate area, public art, misting garden, shelter, restrooms, and a trail connection to MacDonald Woods Park.
places.hours: Normally open sunrise to sunset, but the entire park is closed July 20-August 7, 2026 for repaving. Normal hours resume only after the Town confirms reopening.
places.cost: General park, inclusive playground, misting garden, courts, trail, art, and ordinary picnic access are free when open. The picnic shelter requires a reservation for guaranteed use.
places.parking: Do not use the Thurston Drive park lot during the full repaving closure. After reopening, use 111 Thurston Drive and follow signs for Kids Together Playground and the shelter.
places.restroom: Park restrooms are unavailable during the full closure. After reopening, facilities are located near the developed playground and shelter area.
places.accessibility: Kids Together Playground was designed for integrated play among children with varied physical and developmental abilities. Repaving may affect routes temporarily, so reassess exact access after reopening.
places.trail: A park trail crosses near a stream and small wetland and reaches a pedestrian overpass linking MacDonald Woods Park. All internal routes are unavailable during repaving.
places.family: The inclusive playground's sensory, climbing, imaginative, and social spaces are the main family draw, with Katal the dragon, misting garden, courts, art, shelter, and nearby nature connections.
places.dogs: No recreational access is permitted during the closure. After reopening, keep dogs leashed and away from playground activity, misting features, reserved shelter use, and sensitive stream areas.
places.picnic: Tables and a reservable shelter support family meals when the park is open. The shelter and all picnic access are unavailable during repaving.
places.landmarks: Look for Kids Together Playground, Katal the dragon, inclusive multi-sensory play areas, misting garden, public art, basketball and multi-use slabs, pop-up skate area, and MacDonald Woods overpass.
places.closures: The entire park is closed July 20-August 7, 2026 for repaving. Treat playground, misting garden, restrooms, courts, trail, shelter, and parking as unavailable until the Town posts reopening.

places.name: Black Creek Greenway
places.operator: Town of Cary
places.address: Choose a trailhead for the section you plan to use. Fred G. Bond Metro Park serves the southern hub; Black Creek and Godbold Park trailheads serve the middle; Old Reedy Creek Road normally serves the north but its connecting Phase 3 segment is currently closed.
places.summary: Black Creek Greenway is a 7.1-mile, ten-foot-wide asphalt spine linking Bond Park, Godbold Park, North Cary Park, Lake Crabtree, Reedy Creek, White Oak Creek, neighborhood routes, restrooms, dog and action-sports facilities, and the East Coast Greenway.
places.hours: The greenway is open dawn to dusk where construction and park conditions permit. Connected parks, restrooms, dog park, boathouse, and parking lots use their own hours.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Dog-park passes, boathouse rentals, programs, and nearby facilities are separate.
places.parking: Use Bond Park for the south, Godbold Park or Black Creek Trailhead near Maynard Road for central access, and check construction before using Old Reedy Creek Road. Neighborhood entrances should not be assumed to provide public parking.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at Bond Park, Godbold Park, North Cary Park, and Old Reedy Creek Road Trailhead when those facilities and connecting sections are open.
places.accessibility: The primary route is ten-foot asphalt and supports many wheelchairs and strollers, but Cary warns that some grades may be too steep for wheelchair use. Detours, road crossings, and construction routes vary.
places.trail: The 7.1-mile asphalt route includes creek corridors, underpasses, road crossings, the new Cary Parkway pedestrian bridge, street-side segments, parks, lakes, and links to White Oak and Reedy Creek greenways.
places.family: Choose a short park-to-park or lake segment rather than treating the whole corridor as one outing. Bond Park, North Cary Park, and Godbold Park provide useful family anchors with facilities.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted on the greenway. Cary's fenced dog parks require passes and separate rules; keep dogs leashed until fully inside an authorized off-leash area.
places.picnic: Use tables and shelters at connected parks or Old Reedy Creek Trailhead rather than blocking the greenway. Organized trail events require approval.
places.landmarks: Major connections include Bond Lake and boathouse, White Oak Creek Greenway hub, Battery Lake, Godbold Park, Cary Action Sports, Cary Parkway pedestrian bridge, North Cary Park, Lake Crabtree overlook, and Old Reedy Creek Road.
places.closures: Phase 2 from Livingstone Drive to Weston Parkway has reopened, but Phase 3 from Weston Parkway to Old Reedy Creek Trailhead is closed for renovation and anticipated to reopen in winter 2026. Review the live detour before a through-trip.

places.name: Greenfield Park
places.operator: City of Wilmington Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1739 Burnett Boulevard, Wilmington, NC 28401 is the general park address. Use Amphitheater Drive for ticketed concerts and follow internal signs for playgrounds, skate park, lake loop, fishing dock, shelters, or boat launch.
places.summary: Greenfield Park is a 250-acre lake and recreation destination with a 4.8-mile paved walking and biking loop, accessible fishing dock, age- and ability-specific playgrounds, picnic shelters, restrooms, pickleball, skate park, boat and kayak rentals, birding, and Greenfield Lake Amphitheater.
places.hours: The outdoor park and skate park are open sunrise to sunset. Boat rentals, concessions, amphitheater events, restrooms, and reserved facilities use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, lake loop, skate park, picnic, pickleball, birding, and fishing-dock access are free. Fishing licenses, boat rentals, concessions, reservations, and concerts may charge.
places.parking: Use 1739 Burnett Boulevard for the general park and choose the lot nearest your activity. Concert traffic and event controls can change Amphitheater Drive access and fill nearby spaces.
places.restroom: Restroom facilities and water fountains are available near developed recreation areas. They are not continuous around the 4.8-mile lake loop.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, paved loop, accessible fishing dock, ability-specific playground options, shelters, restrooms, and major park routes provide accessible choices, though individual slopes and event layouts vary.
places.trail: A 4.8-mile paved shared path circles Greenfield Lake for walking and biking. Expect a substantial loop with road approaches, bridges, wildlife, shade variation, and no continuous facilities.
places.family: Families can combine playgrounds, short lake-loop segments, shelters, birding, fishing dock, skate park, picnic areas, and seasonal paddling without committing to the full loop.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled around bicycles, wildlife, playgrounds, docks, events, and narrow path areas. Remove waste and follow posted attraction restrictions.
places.picnic: Picnic shelters and tables support casual and group visits. Reserve a shelter for guaranteed organized use and follow event restrictions near the amphitheater.
places.landmarks: Key destinations include Greenfield Lake and 4.8-mile loop, accessible fishing dock, playgrounds, Greenfield Grind Skate Park, pickleball courts, boat launch and rentals, picnic shelters, and Greenfield Lake Amphitheater.
places.closures: Storms, flooding, wildlife conditions, lake maintenance, events, rentals, and master-plan work can affect separate areas. The amphitheater is operated for events by Live Nation and does not share ordinary park access rules.

places.name: Wilmington Riverwalk
places.operator: City of Wilmington
places.address: The 1.75-mile route runs along the Cape Fear River from Nun Street on the south to the Isabel Holmes Bridge on the north. Orange Street Landing is a useful central historic access point; choose parking for the segment you plan to visit.
places.summary: Wilmington Riverwalk is a 1.75-mile downtown waterfront route linking parks, shops, restaurants, museums, public art, historic interpretation, docks, Battleship North Carolina views, and connections to the River to Sea Bikeway and East Coast Greenway.
places.hours: Use the public Riverwalk according to posted waterfront, construction, docking, and adjacent-property conditions. Shops, museums, restrooms, docks, parks, and events use separate hours.
places.cost: Walking the public Riverwalk is free. Downtown parking, museums, tours, dining, docking, events, and attractions may charge separately.
places.parking: Use a City deck or legal downtown street space near your chosen segment. River Place Deck at 14 Grace Street is central; Market and Second Street decks serve the historic core, while the Convention Center deck serves the north. Rates and event pricing vary.
places.restroom: Restroom availability comes from adjacent public facilities, parks, businesses, museums, and event venues rather than continuous Riverwalk facilities. Plan stops before a full out-and-back.
places.accessibility: Several audited downtown entrances, including Orange Street, Mueter's Alley and Dock Street, have compliant routes and ramps. Deck replacement, temporary detours, steep transitions, docks, crowds, and individual buildings can change the best route.
places.trail: The Riverwalk extends 1.75 miles one way on waterfront decking and developed paths. A full out-and-back is 3.5 miles; construction, crowds, dining activity, and event zones can narrow or redirect sections.
places.family: Families can choose a short central section for river views, boats, public art, food, museums, and historic signs instead of walking the full out-and-back distance.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary public sections subject to posted rules. Keep pets controlled around crowds, restaurant patios, docks, bicycles, events, wildlife, and temporary construction paths.
places.picnic: Use designated public seating and parks without blocking the waterfront route. Food, alcohol, large setups, and events are governed by the exact adjacent property and social-district rules.
places.landmarks: Highlights include Orange Street Landing's Underground Railroad designation, Battleship North Carolina views, historic signs, public art, downtown docks, Riverfront Park, Convention Center area, museums, and the Isabel Holmes Bridge end.
places.closures: A multi-year project begun in 2025 is replacing decking across the Riverwalk. Work zones, temporary detours, events, storms, high water, and maintenance can affect sections; check current project notices before expecting a continuous route.

places.name: Long Leaf Park
places.operator: New Hanover County Parks and Gardens
places.address: 314 Pine Grove Drive, Wilmington, NC 28409. Follow the County's detailed park map for the inclusive playground, splashpad, dog park, shelters, courts, trail, fitness areas, ballfields, gardens, or event lawn.
places.summary: Long Leaf Park is a large county recreation park with an inclusive playground, seasonal splashpad, separate small- and large-dog areas, six reservable shelters, 1.55-mile walking trail, StoryWalk, lighted tennis, ballfields, basketball, outdoor gym, fitness obstacle course, gardens, pond, gazebo, and sand volleyball.
places.hours: The park is open daily 8 a.m.-10 p.m. The splashpad operates May 1-September 30 from 9 a.m.-7:30 p.m.; offices, fields, lights, reservations, and events use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, splashpad, dog park, walking trail, StoryWalk, courts when unreserved, fitness areas, and gardens are free. Shelter, field, wedding, walk and event reservations may charge.
places.parking: Use 314 Pine Grove Drive and select the internal lot nearest your destination. The park is large enough that parking near the ballfields can be inconvenient for the splashpad or garden.
places.restroom: Restrooms are distributed near developed shelter, playground, splashpad, athletic, and picnic areas. Check the detailed map for the closest facility.
places.accessibility: The inclusive playground serves children ages 2-12 of varied abilities. A Liberty wheelchair swing requires a code from the parks office, and a loaner water wheelchair is available for the splashpad by prior contact.
places.trail: The park has a 1.55-mile walking trail that can also be reserved for organized walks and 5Ks. Stay clear of reserved events and use the park map to connect facilities.
places.family: The inclusive playground, seasonal splashpad, StoryWalk, shelters, courts, gardens, fitness areas and dog park offer several visit types. Arrange wheelchair swing or splashpad equipment before arriving when needed.
places.dogs: The free off-leash dog park has separate fenced areas for small and large dogs. Leash dogs outside the designated enclosures and follow County dog-park rules.
places.picnic: Six shelters seat roughly 40-125 people and include varying grills, power, water and restroom proximity. Reserve for guaranteed group use and choose a shelter near the activity you need.
places.landmarks: Key destinations include the inclusive playground and Liberty swing, splashpad, Ninja and fitness areas, dog park, six shelters, StoryWalk, 1.55-mile trail, garden pond and gazebo, tennis courts, and ballfields.
places.closures: Splashpad operation is seasonal and weather or maintenance dependent. Ballfields can be unavailable during baseball season, while reservations, major events, storms and facility work can affect individual areas.

places.name: Halyburton Park
places.operator: City of Wilmington Parks and Recreation
places.address: 4099 South 17th Street, Wilmington, NC 28412. Use the nature-center entrance for exhibits, programs, restrooms, shelters, the 1.3-mile loop, and Gary Shell Cross-City Trail connection.
places.summary: Halyburton Park is a 60-acre natural-heritage and education park preserving rare coastal sandhills, with a Nature and Events Center, 1.3-mile paved accessible loop, wildlife programs, apiary, shelters, and a connection to the Gary Shell Cross-City Trail.
places.hours: Outdoor park access follows posted park hours. The Nature Center is open Monday-Saturday 9 a.m.-5 p.m. March-November and 11 a.m.-4 p.m. December-February; events and programs vary.
places.cost: General park, loop trail, nature viewing, and ordinary center access are free. Programs, camps, shelter reservations, weddings, meetings, and events may charge.
places.parking: Use 4099 South 17th Street for the center and park loop. This is also an official Cross-City Trail parking and restroom stop, so events and popular trail periods can increase demand.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at the Nature and Events Center during operating conditions. Do not assume facilities elsewhere on the loop or along the longer Cross-City Trail.
places.accessibility: A 1.3-mile paved, handicap-accessible perimeter path connects the park and Cross-City Trail. The center and developed areas provide accessible options, while natural habitat edges and temporary work zones vary.
places.trail: The 1.3-mile paved loop circles the preserve and connects to the 15-mile Gary Shell Cross-City Trail. Stay on designated routes to protect the South Wilmington Sandhills habitat.
places.family: Families can use the paved loop, nature exhibits, wildlife and bee programs, seasonal camps, shelters and self-guided observation for a manageable environmental-learning visit.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled on allowed outdoor routes. Protect wildlife, apiary operations, programs, events, shelters and sensitive restored longleaf-pine habitat.
places.picnic: Reservable shelters support gatherings in two daily time blocks. Shelter 1 is currently closed, so choose and confirm another shelter before planning a group visit.
places.landmarks: Look for the Nature and Events Center, South Wilmington Sandhills preserve, 1.3-mile loop, apiary, longleaf-pine restoration, shelters, education areas, and Cross-City Trail connection.
places.closures: Shelter 1 is closed until further notice after a fire. Prescribed restoration work, severe weather, programs, private events, trail maintenance and center schedules can affect other areas independently.

places.name: Empie Park
places.operator: City of Wilmington Parks and Recreation
places.address: 3405 Park Avenue, Wilmington, NC 28403. Follow internal signs for Althea Gibson Tennis Complex, dog park, playground, shelter, basketball, restrooms, or Gary Shell Cross-City Trail.
places.summary: Empie Park is a major active-recreation hub with the 24-court lighted Althea Gibson Tennis Complex, free small- and large-dog areas, playground, basketball, shelter, clubhouse, restrooms, parking, and a Gary Shell Cross-City Trail connection.
places.hours: The outdoor park and dog park are open dawn to dusk. Tennis clubhouse, lighted courts, reservations, tournaments, events, and restrooms can use separate operating schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, basketball, dog park, trail connection, and walk-up tennis court use are free. Reserved tennis courts, tournaments, rentals, programs and events may charge.
places.parking: Use 3405 Park Avenue and select the area closest to tennis, dog park, playground or trail. Tournaments and events can fill the main lots.
places.restroom: Restrooms near the playground are temporarily closed for maintenance. Public restrooms at and adjacent to the Althea Gibson clubhouse remain open; plan the walk before settling at the playground.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, routes, tennis complex, clubhouse, playground, shelter, restrooms, dog park and Cross-City Trail connection provide accessible options, though exact court and event access varies.
places.trail: Empie Park is an official parking and restroom stop on the 15-mile paved Gary Shell Cross-City Trail. Internal paths connect recreation areas to the through-route.
places.family: Families can use the playground, basketball, shelter, trail and tennis areas, but children under 12 are not permitted inside the dog park.
places.dogs: The free fenced dog park has separate large- and small-dog areas, shade, water and waste stations. Children under 12, puppies under four months, food and toys are prohibited; leash dogs entering and leaving.
places.picnic: A picnic shelter and tables support meals and gatherings. Reserve organized use and note that the nearest playground-side restrooms are currently closed.
places.landmarks: The primary destinations are Althea Gibson Tennis Complex and clubhouse, small- and large-dog areas, playground, basketball courts, shelter, and Gary Shell Cross-City Trail connection.
places.closures: Playground-side restrooms are closed until further notice, while clubhouse restrooms remain open. Tournaments, maintenance, storms, reservations and trail work can affect other facilities.

places.name: Gary Shell Cross-City Trail
places.operator: City of Wilmington
places.address: For a central developed trail stop use Halyburton Park at 4099 South 17th Street or Empie Park at 3405 Park Avenue. The 15-mile route runs from Wade Park to the Heide-Trask Drawbridge, so choose access by trip segment.
places.summary: Gary Shell Cross-City Trail is a 15-mile paved multi-use route connecting Wade, Halyburton, Empie and Anne McCrary parks with the Cameron Art Museum, Independence Mall, UNCW, Autumn Hall, shopping areas, the Intracoastal Waterway, local bikeways, and the East Coast Greenway network.
places.hours: Use trail sections during posted daylight and connected-park hours. Parks, restrooms, commercial areas, campus connections, road crossings, and construction zones use separate conditions.
places.cost: General trail access is free. Parking, transit, programs, museums, shopping, rentals and connected attractions may charge separately.
places.parking: Official parking is available at Wade Park, Halyburton Park, Empie Park and Anne McCrary Park. Choose a lot for the segment you intend to use and do not assume a full 15-mile one-way trip has return transportation.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at Wade Park, Halyburton Park and Empie Park, subject to facility conditions. Empie's playground-side restrooms are currently closed, but clubhouse restrooms remain open.
places.accessibility: The trail is designed as an off-road multi-use route for walkers, cyclists, wheelchair users and strollers, but road crossings, slopes, driveway conflicts, detours, bridges and connections vary across 15 miles.
places.trail: The 15-mile route mixes paved greenway segments, park paths, bridges, road-adjacent sections and crossings. Keep right, pass left, announce passes, yield to pedestrians and avoid blocking the path.
places.family: Use a short out-and-back between parks or destinations rather than attempting the full route with children. Halyburton and Empie provide facilities and activity options at practical stopping points.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the trail where permitted. Keep leashes short around bicycles, crossings and crowds, remove waste, and follow separate dog-park rules at Empie.
places.picnic: Use designated areas at connected parks rather than stopping across the trail. Organized rides, runs, walks or gatherings require approval.
places.landmarks: Connections include Wade Park, Halyburton Park, Cameron Art Museum, Independence Mall, Empie Park, Anne McCrary Park, UNCW, Autumn Hall, Lumina Station, Landfall Center and Heide-Trask Drawbridge.
places.closures: Road work, bridge projects, flooding, storms, park closures, utility work and event detours can interrupt sections. Check City notices and the current map before relying on a continuous through-trip.

places.name: James L. Dorton Park
places.operator: City of Concord Parks and Recreation
places.address: 5790 Poplar Tent Road, Concord, NC. Use the main park drive and follow internal signs for playgrounds, shelters, soccer, tennis and pickleball, disc golf, restrooms, or the walking trail.
places.summary: James L. Dorton Park is a renovated 24-acre community park with an 18-hole disc-golf course, three playground areas, walking trail, multipurpose and youth soccer fields, three resurfaced tennis courts striped for pickleball, three shelters, restrooms, bridges, and about 180 parking spaces.
places.hours: The park is open dawn to dusk. Fields, courts, shelters, restrooms, concessions, programs, maintenance areas, and tournaments may use separate schedules or restrictions.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, disc golf, and ordinary walk-up recreation are free. Shelter, field, court, program, tournament, and organized-event reservations may charge.
places.parking: The 2025 renovation expanded the park to about 180 parking spaces. Use the internal area closest to your activity and allow extra time during soccer, disc-golf, court, and shelter events.
places.restroom: A renovated restroom building includes an inclusive adult changing table. Confirm operating conditions before relying on it for a long visit; the concession stand is listed as closed.
places.accessibility: Renovations added pedestrian bridges, improved routes, parking, playground and field updates, and an inclusive adult changing table. Disc-golf terrain, natural slopes, fields, and individual shelter approaches can still vary.
places.trail: A park walking trail connects recreation areas, and two new pedestrian bridges were included in the renovation. The 18-hole disc-golf route is a separate activity corridor; watch for flying discs and field traffic.
places.family: Three playground areas, swings, fields, shelters, courts, walking, and disc golf support varied family visits. Choose parking near the primary activity rather than expecting every feature to be adjacent.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park areas where posted rules permit. Keep pets out of active play, court, and field areas, avoid disc-golf flight paths, and remove waste.
places.picnic: Three reservable shelters provide picnic tables, electricity, and varying grill access. Reserve for guaranteed group use and confirm which shelter is nearest your planned activity.
places.landmarks: Key destinations include the renovated playground, 18-hole disc-golf course, three tennis and pickleball courts, multipurpose field, youth soccer field, three shelters, restroom building, walking trail, and pedestrian bridges.
places.closures: The park reopened after major renovation in 2025. Weather, wet fields, maintenance, reservations, leagues, tournaments, and special events can affect individual facilities; check City notices before organized play.

places.name: Les Myers Park
places.operator: City of Concord Parks and Recreation
places.address: 338 Lawndale Avenue, Concord, NC. Follow internal signs for the playgrounds, courts, ballfield, amphitheater, community building, shelters and gazebos, restrooms, or McEachern Greenway parking.
places.summary: Les Myers Park is a 21-acre community park with two playgrounds, eight tennis courts, four pickleball courts, a baseball and softball field, walking trail, McEachern Greenway access, restrooms, shelters, gazebos, an amphitheater, and the C.T. Sherrill Community Building.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open dawn to dusk. The community building, amphitheater, courts, fields, restrooms, reservations, programs, and events use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, greenway, and ordinary walk-up court access are free. Building, gazebo, shelter, court, field, amphitheater, program, and event reservations may charge.
places.parking: Use the Lawndale Avenue park entrance and choose the internal area nearest your destination. The lot also serves McEachern Greenway and Downtown Loop visitors, so events and league play can increase demand.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are listed among park amenities, and the C.T. Sherrill Community Building has restrooms during authorized use. The concession facility is listed as closed.
places.accessibility: Developed parking and paths serve the community building, amphitheater, shelters, courts, playground areas, and greenway connection, but exact surfaces and event routes vary by destination.
places.trail: A park walking trail connects to the 2.2-mile McEachern Greenway and roughly four-mile Downtown Greenway Loop. Select a short park loop or longer greenway route before starting.
places.family: Two playgrounds, swings, courts, ballfield, trail, shelters, gazebos, and events offer several visit types. Confirm field, court, building, and amphitheater schedules before promising a specific activity.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled on allowed outdoor paths and greenway sections, remove waste, and keep pets away from playgrounds, active courts, fields, buildings, and organized events.
places.picnic: Paul's Kitchen and Bob Baucom shelters plus the Neal Davis and Dai Nippon gazebos provide reservable gathering options with different tables, grills, and utilities. Reserve the exact facility needed.
places.landmarks: Look for Frank Dusch Amphitheater, C.T. Sherrill Community Building, Paul’s Kitchen and Bob Baucom shelters, Neal Davis and Dai Nippon gazebos, two playgrounds, courts, ballfield, and McEachern Greenway access.
places.closures: Reservations, performances, camps, leagues, tournaments, maintenance, wet fields, and severe weather can affect facilities independently. Check the City's current schedule before relying on a court, field, building, or event space.

places.name: Weddington Road Bark Park
places.operator: City of Concord Parks and Recreation
places.address: 8955 Weddington Road, Concord, NC. The park provides separate dog enclosures, a playground, restrooms, and parking for the Hector H. Henry II Greenway and Riverwalk area.
places.summary: Weddington Road Bark Park is a 56-acre community-park site centered on a 1.5-acre large-dog enclosure and 0.5-acre small-dog enclosure, with a playground, restrooms, and access parking for the Hector H. Henry II Greenway and Riverwalk corridor.
places.hours: The park is open dawn to dusk. Dog-lot maintenance, weather, turf recovery, restrooms, playground work, and connected-greenway conditions can change access.
places.cost: General park, dog-area, playground, and greenway access are free. Programs, organized gatherings, or future reservable uses may have separate requirements.
places.parking: Use 8955 Weddington Road and follow signs for the dog lots, playground, restroom, or greenway. The lot also serves trail visitors, so peak dog-walking and event periods can be busy.
places.restroom: Restrooms are listed on the official park page. Hours and temporary maintenance can vary, so do not treat them as continuously available outside normal park conditions.
places.accessibility: Developed parking serves the dog park, playground, restrooms, and greenway access. Gate thresholds, turf, mud, slopes, and the longer connected trail can affect practical accessibility.
places.trail: The park provides access to the Hector H. Henry II Greenway and Riverwalk corridor. Plan the length and return route separately from time inside the dog enclosure.
places.family: The playground offers a non-dog activity, but children require close supervision around parking, gates, unfamiliar dogs, and the separate enclosures. Follow every posted age and entry rule.
places.dogs: Use the 0.5-acre enclosure for small dogs and 1.5-acre enclosure for large dogs. Leash dogs outside the designated lots, supervise continuously, clean up waste, and follow current posted health, behavior, and gate rules.
places.picnic: The official amenity list does not identify a reservable shelter. Use only designated seating or open areas without blocking gates, paths, playground access, or dog-park circulation, and follow posted food rules.
places.landmarks: The principal destinations are the separate small- and large-dog lots, playground, restroom building, parking area, and Hector H. Henry II Greenway and Riverwalk access.
places.closures: The City periodically closes one or both dog lots for turf and facility maintenance. Check current Parks and Recreation notices before travel, especially after prolonged rain or scheduled maintenance.

places.name: McEachern Greenway
places.operator: City of Concord Parks and Recreation
places.address: For a practical southern trailhead use Les Myers Park, 338 Lawndale Avenue; J.W. Mickey McGee Park and Wilson Street Park provide additional official access. The 2.2-mile route follows Three-Mile Branch through central Concord.
places.summary: McEachern Greenway is a 2.2-mile paved central-Concord route following Three-Mile Branch between Les Myers Park and the area north of Wilson Park, with access at McGee and Wilson Street parks, a Downtown Connector, bridges, underpasses, and LifeTrail fitness stations.
places.hours: Use the greenway during posted park and daylight conditions. Connected parks, restrooms, underpasses, construction areas, and downtown facilities use separate schedules and may close for flooding or work.
places.cost: General greenway and connected-park access are free. Parking restrictions, rentals, programs, events, and downtown services may have separate costs.
places.parking: Official trail parking is available at Les Myers Park, J.W. Mickey McGee Park, and Wilson Street Park. Choose a trailhead for your planned segment instead of assuming the full route returns to your vehicle.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at Les Myers and McGee parks during operating conditions. Wilson Street Park has had restroom and trailhead construction, so verify current availability before relying on that stop.
places.accessibility: The developed route is intended for shared walking, rolling, and cycling access, but grades, bridges, underpasses, road crossings, flooding, construction, and park connections vary by segment.
places.trail: The route is about 2.2 miles: roughly one mile from McGee Park to Les Myers Park and 1.2 miles north from McGee to the turnaround beyond Wilson Street. The Downtown Connector and sidewalks create an approximately four-mile loop.
places.family: A short out-and-back from Les Myers or McGee Park pairs trail time with playgrounds, restrooms, and recreation. Supervise children at road crossings, underpasses, bridges, water, and faster bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the greenway where posted rules permit. Keep leashes short around cyclists and crossings, remove waste, and follow separate rules inside connected parks.
places.picnic: Use designated picnic facilities at connected parks rather than stopping across the shared trail. Reserve shelters for guaranteed group use.
places.landmarks: Key connections include Les Myers Park, J.W. Mickey McGee Park, Wilson Street Park, Three-Mile Branch, the Downtown Connector, LifeTrail fitness stations, Corban Avenue and Cabarrus Avenue underpasses, and the Downtown Greenway Loop.
places.closures: Flooding, high water, ice, storms, bridge or underpass work, Wilson Street construction, utility projects, and park closures can interrupt sections. Check current City notices after severe weather.

places.name: Brown Mill Mountain Bike Trail Park
places.operator: City of Concord Parks and Recreation
places.address: Use the official trail parking on 2nd Street SW in Concord. Confirm the live open or closed status before loading bikes because trail conditions can change after rain, snow, ice, or maintenance.
places.summary: Brown Mill Mountain Bike Trail Park provides 4.25 miles of purpose-built mountain-bike trails ranging from beginner to high-skill terrain, with a 2nd Street SW trailhead and condition-based operations coordinated with Tarheel Trailblazers.
places.hours: Ride only during posted daylight and open-trail conditions. This natural-surface system closes when weather, moisture, ice, hazards, maintenance, or utility work could damage trails or endanger users.
places.cost: General trail access is free. Equipment, repairs, instruction, events, and organized activities may have separate costs or approval requirements.
places.parking: Use the designated 2nd Street SW parking area and keep access lanes clear. Do not park on unapproved shoulders, private property, work areas, or trail entrances.
places.restroom: The official trail description does not list a restroom at the trailhead. Plan a restroom stop before arrival and do not rely on nearby private businesses for access.
places.accessibility: This is a natural-surface mountain-bike trail with roots, grades, turns, obstacles, changing soil, and beginner-to-advanced features; it is not a paved accessible greenway. Evaluate the exact loop against rider ability.
places.trail: The system totals 4.25 miles with terrain from beginner to high skill. Review current trail signage, ride within ability, yield appropriately, control speed, wear a helmet, and do not enter closed sections.
places.family: Experienced families should match riders to the beginner sections and supervise closely. The trail is not a conventional playground or paved learn-to-ride loop; inspect features before children commit to them.
places.dogs: This bike-focused trail has fast and sometimes limited-sightline traffic. If dogs are permitted under current posted rules, keep them leashed, controlled, and out of riders' paths; do not assume off-leash use is safe.
places.picnic: The official listing does not identify shelters or developed picnic facilities. Keep the trailhead clear and use a separately listed park for a planned group picnic.
places.landmarks: The destination is the 2nd Street SW trailhead and 4.25-mile beginner-to-high-skill trail network. Trail signs and the live condition report are more useful navigation tools than a single street address alone.
places.closures: Check the Tarheel Trailblazers status before every visit. The City has recently closed Brown Mill for ice, snow, weather, and utility maintenance; never ride around a closure sign even if conditions appear dry at the trailhead.

places.name: Lake Fisher
places.operator: City of Concord Parks and Recreation
places.address: 5099 Lake Fisher Road, Kannapolis, NC. This is a City of Concord water-supply lake with staff-operated jon-boat rentals, not a general swimming, shoreline-fishing, kayak, or private-boat access site.
places.summary: Lake Fisher is a 534-acre City of Concord water-supply lake offering seasonal staff-supported fishing from rentable 14- and 15-foot jon boats, with life jackets, oars, and restrooms; private watercraft, kayaks, swimming, and bank fishing are prohibited.
places.hours: The posted warm-season schedule is Wednesday-Saturday 7 a.m.-3 p.m. and Sunday afternoon, with Monday-Tuesday closed; colder-season hours are weekends only. Weather, water levels, holidays, and operations override the schedule, so call 704-920-5630 before traveling.
places.cost: A free Lake Fisher membership is required for visitors age 18 and older to rent a boat. Per-person jon-boat fees vary by age and City residency; children under 12 ride free with an accompanying adult. Motors, fuel, batteries, and fishing gear are not included.
places.parking: Use the official Lake Fisher facility at 5099 Lake Fisher Road. Arrive with enough time for membership, rental, safety, and equipment steps before the early closing time; never use unauthorized shoreline access.
places.restroom: Restrooms are listed among Lake Fisher amenities during facility operating conditions. They are not available when the lake operation is closed.
places.accessibility: Contact staff before travel to discuss the dock, boat-transfer needs, life jackets, restrooms, and current water level. A jon-boat fishing operation can require balance and transfers not represented by the parking address alone.
places.trail: Lake Fisher is a managed boat-fishing destination, not a public perimeter trail. Shoreline wandering and bank fishing are prohibited to protect the water supply.
places.family: Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult and do not pay the per-person boat fee. Bring age-appropriate gear and confirm current conditions; this is not a swimming, beach, kayak, or casual shoreline-play destination.
places.dogs: The official lake guidance does not present Lake Fisher as a dog-recreation site. Because access centers on small rental boats and protected water-supply rules, contact staff before bringing a pet and use another park when dog activity is the priority.
places.picnic: The official visitor page emphasizes fishing and boat operations rather than reservable picnic facilities. Confirm any allowed shore-based food or gathering plans with staff and protect the water-supply site from litter.
places.landmarks: The essential destination is the staffed rental and launch facility for 14- and 15-foot jon boats. Life jackets and oars are included; visitors supply fishing tackle and any permitted motor, fuel, trolling motor, or battery.
places.closures: The City announced a low-water closure through August 1, 2026, but its page still displays that notice without a newer reopening confirmation. Call 704-920-5630 before travel; water level, weather, Christmas, New Year's Day, and operational conditions can close the facility.

places.name: Salem Creek Greenway
places.operator: City of Winston-Salem Recreation and Parks
places.address: For developed parking, restrooms, and trail access use Washington Park at 1490 South Broad Street or Reynolds Park at 2450 Reynolds Park Road. The route continues 5.2 miles between Marketplace Mall and Salem Lake Park.
places.summary: Salem Creek Greenway is a 5.2-mile, eight-foot-wide paved corridor linking Marketplace Mall, Washington Park, Old Salem, Salem College, WSSU, Happy Hill and Reynolds parks, Long Branch and Peachtree greenways, and Salem Lake Park and Trail.
places.hours: Use the greenway from sunrise to sunset and follow the hours of each connected park. Flooding, construction, events, bridge work, and park operations can close individual sections.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Parking restrictions, rentals, programs, events, and connected attractions may have separate costs.
places.parking: Choose a trailhead for your planned segment. Washington, Happy Hill, Reynolds, and Salem Lake parks provide practical developed access; do not assume a 5.2-mile one-way trip returns to your vehicle.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at several connected parks, including Washington, Happy Hill, Reynolds, and Salem Lake, during facility operating conditions. They are not continuous along the route.
places.accessibility: The principal route is an eight-foot paved shared-use trail, but road crossings, grades, bridges, underpasses, flooding, construction detours, and park connections vary.
places.trail: The 5.2-mile route links to Salem Lake Trail, Strollway, Long Branch Trail, Peachtree Greenway, and other local routes. Plan distance and return transportation before combining corridors.
places.family: A short out-and-back from a park trailhead provides restrooms, play areas, or picnic options. Supervise children around creek edges, road crossings, bridges, underpasses, and faster bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the greenway where posted rules permit. Keep leashes short around cyclists and crossings, remove waste, and follow separate rules in connected parks.
places.picnic: Use designated shelters and picnic areas at connected parks rather than blocking the shared trail. Reserve shelters for guaranteed group use.
places.landmarks: Connections include Washington Park, Gateway Nature Preserve, Old Salem, Salem College, WSSU, Happy Hill Park, Reynolds Park, Salem Lake Park, Strollway, and Long Branch and Peachtree greenways.
places.closures: Creek flooding, storms, races, construction, bridge or utility work, and connected-park closures can interrupt segments. Check current City alerts after heavy rain and before a through-trip.

places.name: High Point City Lake Park
places.operator: City of High Point Parks and Recreation
places.address: 602 West Main Street, Jamestown, NC 27282. Follow the park map for the aquatic center, marina, train and carousel, miniature golf, event center, shelters, playgrounds, Camp Ann, or greenway bridge.
places.summary: High Point City Lake Park is a major lakefront recreation complex with a seasonal aquatic center and splashpad, marina and fishing, train, carousel, miniature golf, pontoon tours, ten reservable shelters, event center, playgrounds, picnic areas, and trail links to PEC and regional greenways.
places.hours: The park and marina list seasonal daily hours, currently 7 a.m.-8 p.m. August 3-September 6. The aquatic center, rides, rentals, tours, event center, shelters, and winter operations have separate schedules.
places.cost: General park and trail access are free. Aquatic-center admission, rides, miniature golf, boat rentals and launches, fishing, tours, shelters, and event rentals charge separate fees.
places.parking: Use 602 West Main Street and follow internal signs to the attraction you need. The aquatic center, marina, rides, shelters, Camp Ann, and event spaces are spread out, and peak summer capacity can fill nearby areas.
places.restroom: Restrooms serve developed recreation areas, and additional trail restrooms are near the Camp Ann parking lot and nearby Piedmont Environmental Center during open hours. Availability varies by season and attraction.
places.accessibility: The aquatic center includes zero-depth entry and accessible locker rooms. Developed attractions and paths provide accessible options, but marina transfers, amusement loading, shelters, trails, and temporary event routes vary.
places.trail: A 0.6-mile City Lake Park Trail crosses the Arnold J. Koonce Jr. City Lake area and connects to PEC, the High Point Greenway, and Bicentennial Greenway.
places.family: The park combines water play, rides, miniature golf, playgrounds, picnics, boating, and trails, but these do not share one schedule or ticket. Check the exact attraction before promising it to children.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed in allowed ordinary park areas, remove waste, and follow posted restrictions around the aquatic center, rides, buildings, marina, playgrounds, events, and rental boats.
places.picnic: Ten reservable shelters seat about 40-600 people, while scattered tables and grills are first come. Reserve early for a guaranteed group site and choose one near the intended attraction.
places.landmarks: Key destinations include the 2026 aquatic center, splashpad, marina, train, carousel, mini golf, pontoon tours, event center, ten shelters, Camp Ann, lake bridge, and greenway connection.
places.closures: Aquatic and amusement seasons, capacity limits, weather, water conditions, maintenance, private events, and marina rules can affect areas independently. Check same-day attraction schedules before travel.

places.name: Piedmont Environmental Center
places.operator: City of High Point Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1220 Penny Road, High Point, NC 27265. This is the central access for the environmental center, 6.6 miles of natural trails, and the junction of High Point and Bicentennial greenways.
places.summary: Piedmont Environmental Center is a nature-education and trail hub with 6.6 miles of natural trails, small-animal exhibits, classrooms, programs, a 70-by-30-foot walk-on North Carolina topographic map, restrooms, and connections to both major greenways and City Lake Park.
places.hours: The building and restrooms are open daily 9 a.m.-5 p.m.; trails are open sunrise to sunset. Classes, school visits, holidays, weather, and maintenance can alter access.
places.cost: General center, exhibit, map, and trail access are free. Classes, camps, group programs, room use, and special events may charge or require registration.
places.parking: Use 1220 Penny Road for the center and trail junction. The nearby Legion Lot at 1102 Penny Road is another greenway access point; do not block program or service areas.
places.restroom: Restrooms are inside the environmental center during its daily 9 a.m.-5 p.m. building hours. Natural trails and longer greenway sections do not have continuous facilities.
places.accessibility: The center and developed greenway access provide accessible options, while the natural-trail network includes roots, slopes, narrow sections, and changing surfaces. Ask staff for the best route for current needs.
places.trail: Six color-marked south-preserve loops and two north-preserve routes total 6.6 miles, ranging from 0.2 to 2.3 miles. Paved High Point and Bicentennial greenways also meet here.
places.family: Animal exhibits, the giant walk-on state map, classes, and short natural loops make a manageable learning visit. Choose a marked loop before starting and carry water for longer combinations.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use allowed outdoor trails under posted rules, but keep pets away from animal exhibits, indoor spaces, classes, sensitive habitat, and other visitors.
places.picnic: Use designated outdoor areas without blocking the center, trail junction, or program spaces. Confirm group plans with staff; the site primarily serves nature education and trail access.
places.landmarks: Look for the environmental-center building, North Carolina Mapscape, small-animal exhibits, Bill Faver Lakeshore Trail, Deep River Trail, color-marked loops, and the two-greenway junction.
places.closures: Natural trails can close or become unsuitable after storms, flooding, ice, or maintenance. Building programs and school groups may affect indoor access; check current notices before a specialized visit.

places.name: Oak Hollow Park
places.operator: City of High Point Parks and Recreation
places.address: Use Oak Hollow Marina at 3431 North Centennial Street for launches, fishing, rentals, playground and staff. Festival Park, Sailboat Point, North Overlook, campground, tennis, and golf have separate entrances around the 1,500-acre complex.
places.summary: Oak Hollow Park is a 1,500-acre recreation complex around an 800-acre water-supply reservoir, with a marina, accessible playground and fishing, boat launches and seasonal rentals, Festival Park, Sailboat Point, North Overlook, campground, golf and tennis facilities, shelters, rowing, and events.
places.hours: Oak Hollow Marina is open daily on a seasonal schedule, currently 7 a.m.-8 p.m. August 3-September 6. Sailboat Point, North Overlook, and Festival Park close 45, 25, and 15 minutes before the marina; other facilities differ.
places.cost: General scenic park access is free. Bank fishing, boat launches and rentals, camping, golf, tennis, shelters, programs, and events charge separate fees; a state fishing license is also required where applicable.
places.parking: Route to the exact sub-area rather than 'Oak Hollow Park.' Use 3431 North Centennial Street for the marina; Festival Park is at 1841 Eastchester Drive, while campground, golf, tennis, overlooks, and Sailboat Point use separate access.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at developed facilities including the marina and Festival Park during operating conditions. Do not assume they are open at every overlook, shoreline area, or after a sub-area's earlier closing time.
places.accessibility: The marina lists an accessible playground, boat launch, bank-fishing area, and fishing pier. Accessibility at shelters, campground, rowing areas, golf, tennis, and shoreline terrain varies by subsite.
places.trail: Oak Hollow is organized around reservoir recreation and distinct park facilities rather than one continuous public shoreline trail. Use the official park map and avoid restricted water-supply areas.
places.family: The accessible playground, fishing pier, Festival Park picnics, paddling, camping, and events support family visits, but swimming in Oak Hollow Lake is prohibited and each subsite has its own schedule.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed in allowed public areas, remove waste, and follow separate rules at the marina, campground, playground, golf, tennis, event, and boating facilities.
places.picnic: Reservable shelters are available at Festival Park, North Overlook, and Sailboat Point. Choose the exact lake view and facility access needed, and note each area closes before the marina.
places.landmarks: The complex includes Oak Hollow Marina, accessible fishing pier and playground, Festival Park and dam, Sailboat Point, North Overlook, campground, golf course, tennis center, rowing areas, and 11-site boat-access fishing trail.
places.closures: The lake will close to motorized launches until 1 p.m. on August 8, 2026 for the High Point Sprint Triathlon; marina and playground remain accessible. Weather, water levels, races, rentals, and maintenance can cause other changes.

places.name: High Point Greenway
places.operator: City of High Point Parks and Recreation
places.address: For the southern endpoint use Armstrong Park; University Park at 1800 Deep River Road, Piedmont Environmental Center at 1220 Penny Road, and Legion Lot at 1102 Penny Road provide additional access along the 4.9-mile route.
places.summary: High Point Greenway is a 4.9-mile paved shared-use route from Armstrong Park through central trailheads to Piedmont Environmental Center and a short City Lake Park connection, where it joins the Bicentennial Greenway and natural-trail network.
places.hours: Use the greenway during daylight and posted connected-park hours. Flooding, boardwalk conditions, construction, storms, maintenance, and events can affect sections.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Connected attractions, programs, events, rentals, and parking restrictions may have separate costs.
places.parking: Access is available at Armstrong Park, Kirkman Park School where permitted, University Park, Piedmont Environmental Center, Legion Lot, and City Lake Park. Choose a segment and return plan before starting.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at Piedmont Environmental Center from 9 a.m.-5 p.m. and at City Lake Park and some connected facilities during operating conditions, not continuously along the route.
places.accessibility: The route is paved and includes long boardwalk sections, but grades, crossings, wet surfaces, construction, and trailhead connections vary. Confirm the segment most appropriate for current mobility needs.
places.trail: Official segment distances total 4.9 miles from Armstrong Park to PEC, plus a 0.4-mile connection toward City Lake Park. Keep right, pass left, and announce bicycle passes.
places.family: Short sections from University Park, PEC, or City Lake Park pair trail time with facilities and activities. Supervise children at road crossings, bridges, boardwalks, water, and bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the trail where posted rules permit. Keep leashes short around cyclists and crossings, remove waste, and follow connected-park rules.
places.picnic: Use designated areas in connected parks rather than blocking the shared path. Reserve shelters for guaranteed group use.
places.landmarks: The route connects Armstrong Park, East Lexington Avenue, University Park, Piedmont Environmental Center, Legion Lot, City Lake Park Trail, and Bicentennial Greenway.
places.closures: Flooding, storms, icy boardwalks, bridge or utility work, construction, and park closures can interrupt segments. Check City trail notices after severe weather.

places.name: Bicentennial Greenway
places.operator: City of High Point and Guilford County
places.address: For the High Point end use Piedmont Environmental Center at 1220 Penny Road. Other official accesses include Jamestown Park at 7041 East Fork Road, Gibson Park at 5207 West Wendover Avenue, 4125 Piedmont Parkway, and Gallimore Dairy Road.
places.summary: The 6.2-mile High Point section of Bicentennial Greenway runs from Piedmont Environmental Center north through Jamestown and Gibson Park to Gallimore Dairy Road, connecting with High Point Greenway for roughly 11.1 continuous miles and toward Greensboro's regional trail network.
places.hours: Use the greenway during daylight and posted trailhead-park hours. Construction, road crossings, flooding, storms, maintenance, and events can alter access.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Programs, connected attractions, events, and parking restrictions may have separate costs.
places.parking: Use PEC, Jamestown Park, Gibson Park, Piedmont Parkway, or Gallimore Dairy Road access for the segment you plan. Confirm legal parking and a return strategy for a long one-way trip.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at PEC from 9 a.m.-5 p.m. and at some connected parks during their operating conditions. Plan as though long intermediate stretches have no facilities.
places.accessibility: The shared-use route is developed, but steeper sections northeast of PEC include stairs with a bicycle wheel channel, and crossings, grades, surfaces, and trailhead routes vary. It is not uniformly step-free end to end.
places.trail: The High Point section is 6.2 miles: 1.1 miles PEC to East Fork Road, 2.2 to Gibson Park, 1.8 to Piedmont Parkway, and 1.1 to Gallimore Dairy Road.
places.family: Choose a short park-to-park out-and-back rather than the full 6.2 miles with children. Account for grades, stairs, road crossings, water, and faster bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the greenway where posted rules permit. Keep leashes short around bicycles and crossings, remove waste, and follow rules at each connected park.
places.picnic: Use designated areas at PEC, Jamestown Park, Gibson Park, or other connected parks rather than stopping across the path. Reserve facilities for organized groups.
places.landmarks: Connections include PEC, High Point Greenway, Jamestown Park, East Fork Road bridge area, Gibson Park, Piedmont Parkway, Gallimore Dairy Road, and the broader Greensboro trail system.
places.closures: Steep and stair sections, construction, road projects, flooding, storms, ice, events, and jurisdiction-specific maintenance can affect the route. Check both City and County notices before a through-trip.
